30岁女教师晚自习时倒地猝死，母亲发声：她每天6:50前进教室，通常22:00离校，这学期与女儿通话时她多次说“好累”

日前，曾在上海尚德实验学校任教的徐思凝（化名），遗体在上海海湾墓园下葬，亲属与师友、学生共40余人来送别。5月11日20时31分，李羽萍（化名）手机弹出女儿的微信语音通话邀请，“阿姨，徐老师晕倒了。”语音那头称自己是女儿学校的老师，随后，换了一个男声称自己是派出所的，让李羽萍和其他亲属一起过去，并记下了家属电话。21时16分，还在路上的李羽萍接到医院电话，被告知，120到学校时，女儿已经没有生命体征。5月11日21时35分，医生宣布徐思凝死亡。据《居民死亡医学证明书》，医生推断，她的直接死亡原因为“猝死（心源性可能）”。这日距离徐思凝的30岁生日还有13天。

徐思凝是河南信阳人，2018年她从华东师范大学毕业，留在上海当老师。2024年6月底到上海尚德实验学校（下称“尚德”）报到教高一数学，2025年秋季后负责教两个班的数学课、当一个班的班主任，教高二时担任备课组长。今年上半年，徐思凝的工作量逐渐增加，除了教数学、当班主任外，还要负责学校开设的初高中衔接班，出题、带班，引导过渡阶段的学生学习，此外，她还在近两个月内上了两节公开课，为数学公开课做的教案改了不下10次，有时改到深夜12点。自进尚德后，作为班主任的徐思凝，要每天6：50前进教室，通常22：00离校。李羽萍记得，去年秋天女儿担心早晨起不来，告诉她：“如果6：20前没发消息说我起来了，一直给我打电话”。这学期女儿与她通话时多次说“好累”。“最近被焦虑和烦躁填满，心理的淤塞甚至蔓延成具体的不适，身体也跟着哪哪都不对劲。”这是5月9日晚八点多徐思凝发的朋友圈；在文末，她安慰自己，“人生亦有命，安能行叹复坐愁？”这也是她生前最后一条朋友圈。

金正恩豪华船队疑再添新船 联合国制裁成效受质疑

尽管朝鲜长期受到联合国制裁，朝鲜领导人金正恩及其家族使用的豪华船队疑似再添新船，引发外界质疑国际制裁能否有效阻止奢侈品流入朝鲜。

韩国卫星影像分析公司SI Analytics发布报告指出，卫星图像显示，朝鲜东部港口城市元山一处私人码头出现一艘此前未曾发现的驳船。该码头据信专门停泊供金正恩家族使用的船只。

报告指出，金正恩家族原本主要使用六艘船，包括两艘大型豪华游艇、三艘驳船及一艘供游泳活动使用的船只。新发现的驳船在大小和外形上与现有船只相似，可能用于替换长期停泊在金正恩松涛园别墅附近的一艘老旧驳船。

分析认为，新船可能作为金正恩家族的私人休闲场所，也可能用于招待外国贵宾及朝鲜高级官员。金正恩还可能借助这些专属娱乐设施笼络统治精英，巩固忠诚。

报告质疑，联合国对朝鲜实施的奢侈品禁运是否有效，并推测中国和俄罗斯可能通过直接支持或默许，让相关物资流入朝鲜。

不过，报告并未确认新船建造材料的来源，也无法确定是否涉及违反联合国制裁。朝鲜自2006年起因核武器及弹道导弹计划受到联合国安理会制裁，包括禁止供应奢侈品。

另一方面，卫星图像显示，朝鲜今年7月开放的元山葛麻海岸旅游区已基本结束夏季营运。自9月底以来，区内车辆活动大幅减少，约1200把沙滩遮阳伞及其他娱乐设施也已撤除。

SI Analytics估计，尽管朝鲜积极向中国和俄罗斯游客推介旅游区，今年赴朝外国游客仍不足1000人。

胡锡进吁民众少网购多逛商场 网民反问没钱怎么买？

官媒《环球时报》前总编辑胡锡进呼吁民众减少网购，每周至少到实体商场消费一次。部分网民反驳，当前消费疲弱主要源于收入下降和经济压力，而非民众不愿逛商场。

胡锡进星期天（11月22日）在微博发文，询问网民：“你家购物的九成左右，是不是都来自网上？”贴文还配上胡锡进逛商场的视频。

他建议，民众周末多去商场逛逛，至少将三四成购物开支留给实体商场，每周最少去一次，而不是把所有消费都转移至网络平台。

胡锡进认为，随着越来越多人习惯网购，实体商场和步行街逐渐冷清，部分商场可能倒闭。他也提醒，如果周边商场纷纷关闭，街头繁荣会降级，拖累附近住宅价格。

有关言论迅速引发网络讨论。一些网民支持胡锡进，认为网购普及确实冲击实体商业，也使城市街头失去往日的热闹氛围。若超市和商场陆续关门，不仅影响居民购物便利，也可能削弱社区活力。

不过，更多质疑声聚焦于当前的经济压力。有网民直言，并非不愿意逛商场，而是收入减少、消费能力下降，即使到商场也未必有钱购物。“兜里有余裕，谁不愿意舒服地在线下逛买？”

一名自称顺丰同城骑手的网民说，随着配送单价下降，自己的日收入从过去约400元减少至300元，消费也变得更加谨慎。他认为，收入减少才是民众不敢消费的重要原因。

针对胡锡进有关商场倒闭可能拖累房价的说法，部分网民则持相反看法，认为房地产市场低迷和房贷压力才是抑制消费的原因。

有网民总结，与其说人们不愿意逛商场，不如说他们如今真的买不起。也有人说，自己即使走进商场，往往也只是逛一圈，并不会实际消费。

北大数学天才“韦神”再获奖 曾破解近140年数学难题

中国北京大学数学天才、被网民称为“韦神”的韦东奕，荣获2025年度北京市杰出青年中关村奖。他长期从事偏微分方程研究，曾与合作者解决一道悬而未决近140年的数学难题。

综合中国《光明日报》《新京报》星期一（11月23日）报道，2025年度北京市科学技术奖上星期五（11月20日）正式揭晓，北京大学数学科学学院长聘副教授、研究员韦东奕获颁杰出青年中关村奖。

北京大学作为第一完成单位，共获得10项北京市科学技术奖项目奖，包括六项一等奖及四项二等奖。

除了韦东奕，北京大学肿瘤医院研究员朱华、先进制造与机器人学院教授李忠奎，也获得杰出青年中关村奖。

公开资料显示，现年35岁的韦东奕主要从事偏微分方程理论研究，研究方向涵盖流体力学方程、随机矩阵及非线性波动方程。

他长期致力于偏微分方程与流体力学稳定性的理论研究，在多个长期未获解决的数学问题上取得突破，并与合作者解决管道泊肃叶流（Poiseuille flow）在高雷诺数条件下的线性稳定性问题。这是一道存在近140年的数学难题。

韦东奕1991年出生于山东济南，高中时期曾连续两届在国际数学奥林匹克竞赛中获得满分金牌。2010年，他获保送进入北京大学，2014年取得学士学位，2018年获得博士学位。

博士毕业后，韦东奕留在北京大学从事研究工作，2019年12月起担任数学科学学院助理教授，并于今年2月获聘长聘副教授。

韦东奕2021年接受媒体采访时，因手提一瓶矿泉水和两个馒头的朴素形象走红网络。随着他的数学研究经历受到关注，网民开始称他为“韦神”。

items.body:
EMILY STEEL, KALLEY HUANG, RYAN MAC, TRIPP MICKLE2026年11月23日

英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋去年在华盛顿的一场公司活动上。 Eric Lee for The New York Times

As Nvidia became wealthier and wealthier in recent years, Jensen Huang grew increasingly frustrated with his staff.

近年来，随着英伟达日益富有，黄仁勋对员工的不满也与日俱增。

He told groups of subordinates that they had become so rich that he couldn’t motivate them simply with money, according to three people who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss confidential conversations. The only way he could grind more work out of them, he added, was through humiliation.

据三位因讨论保密对话而要求匿名的人士透露，他曾对许多下属表示，他们已经太富有了，以至于他无法仅仅用金钱来激励他们。他还说，能从他们身上榨取更多工作成果的唯一方法就是通过羞辱。

This was an extension of a philosophy that went back decades. Mr. Huang had for years been berating his employees, documents and interviews show. His tongue lashings were savage and inventive. He told one executive that his mother should have aborted him, according to one witness. He said he would rip both arms off a subordinate and beat the person over the head to death with them. And he told another employee he would rip off the top of their head and “pee on your brain.”

这是其可追溯至几十年前的管理理念的延伸。文件和采访显示，黄仁勋多年来一直斥责员工。他的严厉斥责既野蛮又花样百出。据一位目击者称，他曾对一位高管说，他母亲当年就该把他打掉。他说他会扯下某位下属的双臂，用它们来敲打他的头，把他活活打死。他还对另一位员工说，他会掀开他们的头盖骨，“在你的脑子上撒尿”。

The tirades were a centerpiece of the culture at Nvidia throughout its meteoric rise to a $5 trillion company and cornerstone of the artificial intelligence revolution. They were also foundational to Mr. Huang’s management style.

在英伟达迅猛崛起为一家市值5万亿美元的公司并成为人工智能革命基石的过程中，这些斥责成为其企业文化的核心。它们也是黄仁勋管理风格的基础。

“I’d rather torture you into greatness, because I believe in you,” he once said.

“我宁愿用折磨来让你成就伟大，因为我相信你，”他曾说。

He has long used humiliation as a tool, excoriating employees in front of their peers with insults, personal attacks and violent comments, while telling them it was good for them or for the business, according to more than a dozen current and former employees, who spoke on the condition of anonymity for fear of reprisal, and to a review of hundreds of pages of court records and other documents spanning more than 20 years. The behavior kept Nvidia’s human resources department busy fielding workplace complaints, but some employees said the department did not take them seriously.

据十多名因害怕报复而要求匿名的现任和前任员工透露，以及对时间跨度超过20年的数百页法庭记录和其他文件的查阅显示，他长期以来一直将羞辱作为一种工具，在同事面前用侮辱、人身攻击和暴力言论严厉批评员工，同时告诉他们，这对他们自己或对公司有好处。这种行为让英伟达人力资源部忙于处理职场投诉，但一些员工表示该部门并未认真对待这些投诉。

Mr. Huang also inspired love and reverence from many of his employees. Thousands have signed a letter asking for his return. Some have tattoos of Nvidia’s logo. Both those who liked Mr. Huang and those who disliked him described Nvidia as cultish. He cultivated loyalty through not just his technical mastery but also acts of personal compassion and praise. But he ruled through fear.

黄仁勋也赢得了许多员工的爱戴与崇敬。数千人签署了一封要求他回归的联名信。有些人在身上纹了英伟达标志。无论喜欢还是反感黄仁勋的人，都形容英伟达带有狂热崇拜色彩。他不仅通过技术专长，还通过个人的共情举动和赞扬来培养忠诚度。但他通过恐惧进行统治。

Mr. Huang’s behavior began long before Nvidia became one of the most valuable companies in the world. In at least two cases originating in the mid-2000s, the company struck settlements with former senior leaders, both of whom had raised concerns about Mr. Huang’s conduct, saying it was unlawful and exposed Nvidia to liability.

黄仁勋的这种行为早在英伟达成为全球最具价值的公司之一之前就已开始。在至少两起发生于2000年代中期的事件中，该公司与前高管达成了和解，两人均对黄仁勋的行为提出过担忧，称其不合法，使英伟达面临法律责任。

Michael Winston, a former senior vice president of human resources, threatened to sue Nvidia in 2005, saying that he had been fired after objecting to Mr. Huang’s conduct, which he described as “the most verbally abusive, threatening and intimidating behavior” he had witnessed in his career. Mr. Huang “thinks he can get away with anything,” Mr. Winston wrote in notes he made around that time, which were reviewed by The New York Times.

前人力资源高级副总裁迈克尔·温斯顿在2005年曾威胁起诉英伟达，称他在反对黄仁勋的行为后被解雇，他将这些行为描述为他在职业生涯中见过的“最具言语辱骂、威胁和恐吓性质的行为”。黄仁勋“认为他可以为所欲为而不用承担后果”，温斯顿在当时的笔记中写道，《纽约时报》查阅了这些笔记。

迈克尔·温斯顿，摄于2011年。

Nvidia reached a confidential settlement agreement with Mr. Winston for more than $1 million, which has not been previously reported.

英伟达与温斯顿达成了一项超过100万美元的保密和解协议，此事此前未见报道。

Mr. Huang resigned from Nvidia last week, after revelations of multiple extramarital relationships, including one with a subordinate and another with a woman whom U.S. intelligence believes to be a Chinese intelligence asset. But his imprint remains on the culture of the company he co-founded in 1993.

在被曝出与多人——包括与一名下属以及与一名被美国情报部门认为是中国情报线人的女子——存在婚外情之后，黄仁勋上周从英伟达辞职。但他依然在这家他于1993年联合创立的公司的文化上留有印记。

Some managers followed Mr. Huang’s lead, six current and former employees said — including his own daughter, Madison, who as his de facto chief of staff often yelled at people, including executives senior to her. (She continues to work at Nvidia.)

六名现任和前任员工表示，一些管理人员效仿了黄仁勋的做法——包括他本人的女儿黄敏珊，她作为他事实上的幕僚长经常对他人大吼大叫，包括对职级比她高的高管。（她目前仍在英伟达工作。）

Mr. Huang denied Mr. Winston’s allegations in a statement from his spokesman, John Fisher, saying they are from an employee who was fired. They are “fabrications that are now impossible to disprove specifically, and the thousands of Nvidia employees who continue to speak out for Jensen show they’re false,” Mr. Fisher said. Mr. Fisher declined to answer other questions regarding Mr. Huang’s behavior.

黄仁勋通过其发言人约翰·费舍尔发表声明，否认了温斯顿的指控，称这些指控来自一名被解雇的员工。费舍尔表示，这些是“现在无法具体证伪的捏造，成千上万继续为黄仁勋发声的英伟达员工证明了这些是虚假的”。费舍尔拒绝回答有关黄仁勋行为的其他问题。

Nvidia declined to comment. Its board and Colette Kress, its interim chief executive, must now decide if the company will continue in the mold of Mr. Huang or forge a new way forward. She will do so in the face of pressure from Mr. Huang and his supporters, who are agitating for his return to the company. Mr. Huang once belittled Ms. Kress in a meeting with top executives, The Wall Street Journal reported.

英伟达拒绝置评。其董事会和临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯现在必须决定，公司是继续维持黄仁勋的模式，还是开辟一条新的前进道路。她将在黄仁勋及其支持者的压力下做出决定，这些人正在鼓动他重返公司。据《华尔街日报》报道，黄仁勋曾在一个高管会议上贬低过克雷斯。

Harvey C. Jones, the chair of Nvidia’s board, said Tuesday that it “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as C.E.O.” Earlier this month, the board opened an investigation into Mr. Huang.

英伟达董事会主席哈维·C·琼斯上周二表示，董事会“不打算恢复黄仁勋的首席执行官职务”。本月早些时候，董事会对黄仁勋展开了调查。

‘It Pained Me’

“让我痛苦”

Silicon Valley has a long history of founders and chief executives with caustic management styles. Steve Jobs, the co-founder and chief executive of Apple, was infamous for screaming at and insulting employees who did not meet his exacting standards. He was also beloved. Employees credited his approach with helping to create culture-changing products like the iPod and iPhone.

硅谷长期以来一直存在以刻薄风格执掌企业的创始人和首席执行官。苹果公司联合创始人兼首席执行官史蒂夫·乔布斯就因对着未能达到其严格标准的员工大喊和侮辱而臭名昭著。他也深受爱戴。员工们认为他的方法帮助创造了iPod和iPhone等带来文化巨变的产品。

Mr. Huang had a similar effect on his staff. He created a flat organizational structure where he interacted with employees at almost every level of the business. He impressed them with his vision for the future of technology, his command of business strategy and the speed at which he tackled and seemed to conquer new areas of importance, leading the company to the forefront of the A.I. boom.

黄仁勋对他的员工产生了类似的影响。他创建了一个扁平的组织结构，据此与公司几乎各个层级的员工进行互动。他对未来技术的愿景、对商业战略的把控，以及他处理并似乎征服重要新领域的速度，给员工留下了深刻印象，引领公司走到了人工智能热潮的前沿。

Many of the company’s senior leaders have worked for Mr. Huang for more than a decade. Some shared Mr. Huang’s belief that mediocrity should be stamped out and excellence pursued, said four current and former employees. If employees didn’t like it, they could leave.

该公司的许多高管已为黄仁勋工作了十多年。四名现任和前任员工表示，一些人认同黄仁勋的信念，即应消除平庸并追求卓越。如果员工不喜欢这样，他们可以离开。

But in the eyes of some, Mr. Huang’s behavior was extreme, even by Silicon Valley standards.

但在一些人看来，即使以硅谷的标准衡量，黄仁勋的行为也是极端的。

众所周知，黄仁勋从不进行一对一会面，而是更喜欢进行小组会面。

In September 2004, Mr. Winston joined Nvidia to lead human resources. A longtime human resources executive who previously worked at Merrill Lynch and Motorola, Mr. Winston was soon taken aback by the disarray of the H.R. department and the cultural norms of Nvidia. This account of his time at the company is based on interviews and Mr. Winston’s notes and emails, as well as drafts of a lawsuit and other legal documents reviewed by The Times.

2004年9月，温斯顿加入英伟达负责领导人力资源工作。作为一名前美林证券和摩托罗拉的资深人力资源高管，温斯顿很快对人力资源部的混乱状态和英伟达的文化规范感到吃惊。关于他在该公司任职期间的这段记述基于采访以及温斯顿的笔记和电子邮件，还有《纽约时报》查阅的诉讼草案和其他法律文件。

In his first days at Nvidia, he learned that two key human resources leaders had just quit and others were on the verge of resigning.

在英伟达的最初几天，他了解到两名关键的人力资源负责人刚刚辞职，而其他人也处于辞职边缘。

That October, at a two-day off-site meeting attended by about 50 employees, Mr. Winston said Mr. Huang unleashed graphic violent threats.

那年10月，在约50名员工参加的一次为期两天的外出会议上，温斯顿称黄仁勋发出了露骨的暴力威胁。

“You have to do this, or I will rip your fucking heart out and stomp on it,” Mr. Huang said at one point.

“你必须这样做，否则我会把你他妈的心脏挖出来踩在脚下，”黄仁勋一度说。

“I watched them helpless, as they were publicly humiliated, indeed tormented, for extended periods of time, by this lunatic!” Mr. Winston said in his notes. “It pained me physically, intellectually and emotionally to be in the room.”

“我看着他们无助地被这个疯子公开羞辱，甚至是被长时间地折磨！”温斯顿在他的笔记中写道。“待在这个房间里让我在身体、理智和情感上都感到痛苦。”

Mr. Winston said other attendees were “terrorized” and pleaded with him to intervene. Days later, he voiced his concerns during a meeting with top executives. One told him that the conduct was typical but could be a liability for the company. Another advised him to “toughen up.”

温斯顿表示，其他与会者被“吓坏了”，并恳求他介入。几天后，他在一次高管会议上表达了他的担忧。有人告诉他这种行为很典型，但可能成为公司的法律隐患。另一人建议他“强硬点”。

Mr. Winston said he then confronted Mr. Huang, warning him that he had “crossed the line” and that mistreating employees could expose Nvidia to lawsuits. He said Mr. Huang dismissed the concerns and defended public humiliation as a “rite of passage.” Mr. Winston said Mr. Huang bragged to him that he subjected new employees to it during their first six months at the company to test whether they would stand for it.

温斯顿称他随后与黄仁勋对质，警告他已经“越线”，虐待员工可能会使英伟达面临诉讼。他说黄仁勋对这些担忧不予理会，并为公开羞辱辩护，称其为一种“成年礼”。温斯顿称黄仁勋向他吹嘘，他在新员工入职的前六个月里让他们经受这种对待，以测试他们是否能够忍受。

Mr. Winston said Mr. Huang told him that he would not stop. “It has good entertainment value,” Mr. Huang told him.

温斯顿表示，黄仁勋告诉他，他不会停止。“这具有很好的娱乐价值，”黄仁勋告诉他。

That November, Mr. Winston was called into a meeting with Mr. Huang and another executive, who then fired him. Mr. Huang told Mr. Winston that he was “not a good fit.” If Mr. Winston sued Nvidia, Mr. Huang said he would make sure Mr. Winston never worked in Silicon Valley again.

那年11月，温斯顿被叫去参加与黄仁勋和另一名高管的会议，随后该高管解雇了他。黄仁勋告诉温斯顿他“不合适”。黄仁勋表示，如果温斯顿起诉英伟达，他将确保温斯顿永远无法再在硅谷工作。

“To say Nvidia fired me because it just was not ‘a fit’ is nothing more than a smokescreen,” Mr. Winston said in his notes. “The real issue,” he wrote, was Mr. Huang’s “unconscionable behavior.”

“说英伟达解雇我是因为不‘合适’，这不过是烟雾弹，”温斯顿在他的笔记中写道。他写道，“真正的问题”是黄仁勋“肆无忌惮的行为”。

In the months that followed, Mr. Winston filed a formal complaint against Nvidia with California’s Department of Fair Employment and Housing, making allegations that he was fired for opposing Mr. Huang’s treatment of employees, including what he said constituted sexual harassment. Mr. Winston then drafted a lawsuit against Nvidia and Mr. Huang.

在接下来的几个月里，温斯顿向加利福尼亚州公平就业和住房部提交了针对英伟达的正式投诉，指称他因反对黄仁勋对待员工的方式而被解雇，其中包括他称之为构成性骚扰的行为。温斯顿随后起草了针对英伟达和黄仁勋的诉讼。

温斯顿向加利福尼亚州公平就业和住房部提交的投诉副本。

But before the complaint was filed, both sides reached a settlement. Neither side admitted liability or wrongdoing.

但在提交诉状之前，双方达成了和解。双方均未承认责任或不当行为。

Mr. Winston rejoined the banking industry, and later blew the whistle against Countrywide Financial Corporation for its conduct during the buildup to the financial crisis. He died earlier this year.

温斯顿回到了银行业工作，后来对美国全国金融公司在金融危机酝酿期间的行为进行了举报。他于今年早些时候去世。

In 2007, Stephen Pettigrew, a former lawyer for the company, sued Nvidia over claims that included age discrimination and retaliation for reporting Mr. Winston’s allegations of sexual harassment. Mr. Pettigrew reported in a complaint filed with the California Department of Fair Employment and Housing that he sought “emergency medical attention for severe nervous tension and anxiety, as a direct result of the actions of Nvidia.”

2007年，前公司律师斯蒂芬·佩蒂格鲁起诉英伟达，诉求包括年龄歧视以及因报告温斯顿所称的性骚扰指控而遭到报复。佩蒂格鲁在向加利福尼亚州公平就业和住房部提交的投诉中报告说，他寻求“针对严重的神经紧张和焦虑的紧急医疗救助，这直接源于英伟达的行为”。

Mr. Pettigrew discussed Mr. Winston’s complaint during depositions for his own lawsuit, citing Mr. Winston’s allegations as evidence of misconduct that exposed Nvidia to legal risk. Nvidia’s general counsel at the time, David Shannon, confirmed during another deposition in the case that Mr. Winston’s dispute was resolved in a pre-litigation financial settlement.

佩蒂格鲁在为自己的诉讼作证时讨论了温斯顿的投诉，将温斯顿的指控作为英伟达不当行为的证据，该行为使英伟达面临法律风险。英伟达当时的总法律顾问戴维·香农在该案的另一次作证中证实，温斯顿的争议是通过诉前财务和解解决的。

Nvidia denied all wrongdoing, and said that Mr. Pettigrew was fired for poor performance. The company countersued, saying that he breached his contract and misused company documents. The case ultimately settled out of court in 2009.

英伟达否认所有不当行为，并称佩蒂格鲁因表现不佳而被解雇。该公司提起反诉，称他违反了合同并滥用公司文件。该案件最终于2009年在庭外和解。

‘Thank You, Jensen’

“谢谢你，黄仁勋”

After Nvidia’s chips were used in 2012 to train an early artificial intelligence system, Mr. Huang concluded that the future of computing would be A.I. Employees recall receiving his email on a Friday saying the company was pivoting its business from graphics to deep learning, a precursor to A.I. He froze hiring for anybody but experts in that field, and Nvidia became an A.I. chipmaker overnight.

2012年，英伟达的芯片被用于训练一个早期人工智能系统后，黄仁勋得出结论，计算的未来属于人工智能。员工们回忆曾在一个周五收到他的电子邮件，称公司正在将业务重心从图形处理转向深度学习——人工智能的前身。他冻结了该领域专家之外的所有招聘，英伟达一夜之间成为了一家人工智能芯片制造商。

A decade later, Mr. Huang’s bet paid off when ChatGPT arrived, kick-starting frenzied interest and investment in A.I. Demand for Nvidia’s chips skyrocketed, and the company’s value soared. Many of the company’s 42,000 employees became fabulously wealthy and were exhilarated to be at the forefront of a technology Mr. Huang referred to as the next Industrial Revolution.

十年后，黄仁勋的押注得到了回报，ChatGPT的出现引发了对人工智能的狂热兴趣和投资。对英伟达芯片的需求飙升，公司市值暴涨。该公司42000名员工中的许多人变得极其富有，并且对自己能处于这项被黄仁勋称为下一次工业革命的技术最前沿感到振奋。

In the wake of Mr. Huang’s resignation, some employees have shared stories of a boss who went out of his way to support them. Last week, Vartika Singh, who works on strategy at Nvidia, recalled Mr. Huang’s support when her sister had brain cancer.

在黄仁勋辞职后，一些员工分享了这位老板曾不遗余力地支持他们的故事。上周，在英伟达从事战略工作的瓦尔蒂卡·辛格回忆，在她的姊妹患脑癌时，黄仁勋曾给予支持。

“Thank you, Jensen,” Ms. Singh wrote in a social media post. “For your guidance, for believing in people and ideas long before the rest of us understood them, and above all, for your extraordinary humanity.”

“谢谢你，黄仁勋，”辛格在一篇社交媒体帖子中写道。“感谢你的指导，感谢你在我们其他人理解之前就相信了这些人和这些想法，最重要的是，感谢你非凡的仁慈之心。”

Mr. Huang’s mix of disparagement and motivation created something akin to Stockholm syndrome, six current and former employees said. The phenomenon, in which somebody held captive develops an emotional bond with their abuser, mirrored their relationship with Mr. Huang, they said.

六名现任和前任员工表示，黄仁勋这种贬低与激励的混合方式制造了类似于斯德哥尔摩综合征的氛围。他们表示，这种被囚禁者对施虐者产生情感联系的现象恰恰能反映他们与黄仁勋之间的关系。

Rather than fire people, Mr. Huang sometimes preferred to further humiliate them. When Ned Finkle, his former vice president of strategic marketing, faltered in a meeting with a major customer, Mr. Huang chewed him out in front of executives from the other company, said two people who spoke anonymously about the private exchange.

相较于解雇员工，黄仁勋有时更喜欢进一步羞辱他们。两名匿名谈论私下交流的人士表示，当前战略营销副总裁内德·芬克尔在与一位重要客户的会议中表现不佳时，黄仁勋当着另一家公司的高管的面将他痛骂了一顿。

Mr. Huang then named Mr. Finkle vice president of external affairs, or government relations. At the time, Mr. Huang considered it one of the least important jobs at Nvidia, the two people said. Mr. Finkle did not respond to requests for comment.

随后，黄仁勋任命芬克尔为外部事务（即政府关系）副总裁。两名人士表示，当时黄仁勋认为这是英伟达最不重要的工作之一。芬克尔未对置评请求作出回应。

Power Plays

权力博弈

Mr. Huang’s tirades continued until the end.

黄仁勋的长篇大论斥责一直持续到最后。

He usually did not meet one-on-one with subordinates because, he has publicly said, such meetings reduced transparency within Nvidia. But top executives considered the move a power play that gave Mr. Huang more control. If anyone disagreed with Mr. Huang, they would have to do so in front of a group. Mr. Huang could then fire back, ridiculing that person in front of everyone else.

他通常不与下属进行一对一会面，因为正如他曾公开表示的那样，这种会面降低了英伟达内部的透明度。但高层管理人员认为此举是一种权力博弈，赋予了黄仁勋更多的控制权。如果有人不同意黄仁勋的观点，他们将不得不在团队面前表达出来。黄仁勋随后可以反击，在所有人面前嘲笑那个人。

Mr. Huang also ripped into longtime leaders in front of their own teams, telling them their boss was incompetent and unqualified, two people said.

这两名人士表示，黄仁勋还会在老牌高管自己的团队面前对他们进行猛烈抨击，告诉团队成员其上司无能且不称职。

In one instance, Mr. Huang went around a room, telling managers he would kill them, according to one person with knowledge of the incident. When he reached a person in their 70s, Mr. Huang said that the person was really old and everyone hoped they would drop dead.

据一名知情人士称，在一次类似情况中，黄仁勋在会议室里走来走去，告诉经理们自己会杀了他们。当他走到一位70多岁的人面前时，黄仁勋说这个人已经很老了，大家都希望这人赶紧死掉。

Mr. Huang also made personal attacks. He once made fun of an executive who had taken his children camping and said he needed to find a more committed employee for the job, according to one person. He often mocked another executive for enjoying aviation as a hobby, two people said.

黄仁勋还进行人身攻击。据一位知情人士称，他曾取笑一位带孩子去露营的高管，并表示他需要为这个职位寻找一位更投入的员工。两名人士表示，他经常嘲笑另一位高管将航空作为爱好。

In 2019, after Nvidia lost a bid to help build a U.S. government supercomputer, Mr. Huang castigated a sales executive in front of government officials for missing out on part of a contract worth hundreds of millions of dollars. The executive then threw his employee badge at Mr. Huang, who said he accepted the executive’s resignation on the spot, according to two people with knowledge of the incident.

2019年，英伟达在竞标协助建造美国政府超级计算机项目中落选后，黄仁勋当着政府官员严厉斥责了一名销售主管，因为该主管错失了价值数亿美元合同的一部分。据两名知情人士称，该高管随后将员工工牌扔向黄仁勋，黄仁勋当场表示接受该高管的辞呈。

Mr. Huang’s behavior rubbed off on other senior leaders at the company, including his daughter, Madison. On one call last year with Nvidia’s marketing team, Ms. Huang repeatedly berated a vice president, who then left the call, according to a recording of the meeting reviewed by The Times.

黄仁勋的行为也影响了公司其他高级领导人，包括他的女儿黄敏珊。根据《纽约时报》查阅的一份会议录音，在去年一次与英伟达营销团队的通话中，黄敏珊一再斥责一名副总裁，该副总裁随后退出了通话。

“I’m having an anxiety attack,” the vice president said. “I’m going to drop off. I’m sorry.”

“我焦虑发作了，”该副总裁说。“我要退出了。抱歉。”

Ms. Huang did not respond to requests for comment.

黄敏珊未对置评请求作出回应。

As Nvidia became the linchpin of the A.I. boom, Mr. Huang’s conduct started to spill outside the company. At Nvidia’s developer conference earlier this year, Mr. Huang moderated a panel with business partners, including Arthur Mensch, the chief executive of the French A.I. start-up Mistral.

随着英伟达成为人工智能热潮的核心，黄仁勋的行为开始蔓延到公司之外。在今年早些时候的英伟达开发者大会上，黄仁勋主持了一场与商业伙伴的讨论会，其中包括法国人工智能初创公司Mistral的首席执行官阿瑟·门施。

Mistral联合创始人兼首席执行官阿瑟·门施3月在圣何塞的一场由黄仁勋主持的座谈会上。

During the panel, Mr. Huang interrupted Mr. Mensch, taking issue with the Mistral chief executive’s French accent, according to footage of the talk.

根据该谈话的视频，在讨论会期间，黄仁勋打断了门施，对这位Mistral首席执行官的法国口音表示不满。

“I want to say it in human words,” Mr. Huang said, after Mr. Mensch tried to explain an A.I. concept. A spokesman for Mistral declined to comment.

“我想用人话来说，”在门施试图解释一个人工智能概念后，黄仁勋说道。Mistral发言人拒绝置评。

Daniel Gutierrez, an A.I. researcher and longtime “Jensen fan” who was watching the panel, said the interaction changed his perspective on Mr. Huang.

当时观看讨论会的人工智能研究员、资深“黄仁勋粉丝”丹尼尔·古铁雷斯表示，这次互动改变了他对黄仁勋的看法。

“I thought in the moment, what is happening right now that’s causing you to attack this poor guy?” Mr. Gutierrez said. “When all the new stuff happened in the last week, I go, wait a minute now. Maybe Jensen isn’t the guy I thought I revered.”

“我当时想，到底发生了什么，让你攻击这个可怜的家伙？”古铁雷斯说。“当上周发生所有这些新事情时，我想，等一下。也许黄仁勋并不是我曾以为我尊敬的那个人。”

Emily Steel是一名调查记者，为《纽约时报》报道商业新闻。她曾揭露多家大型公司内部的性骚扰行为，最近主要关注网约车行业。

Kalley Huang是时报驻旧金山记者，报道科技行业和业内大型公司，包括英伟达和苹果。

Ryan Mac报道全球科技行业的企业责任相关议题。

Tripp Mickle报道英伟达、谷歌和苹果等全球最大的科技公司。他也报道整个科技行业的趋势，包括裁员、生成式AI和机器人出租车等。

blocks.text: EMILY STEEL, KALLEY HUANG, RYAN MAC, TRIPP MICKLE2026年11月23日
英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋去年在华盛顿的一场公司活动上。 Eric Lee for The New York Times
As Nvidia became wealthier and wealthier in recent years, Jensen Huang grew increasingly frustrated with his staff.
近年来，随着英伟达日益富有，黄仁勋对员工的不满也与日俱增。

He told groups of subordinates that they had become so rich that he couldn’t motivate them simply with money, according to three people who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss confidential conversations. The only way he could grind more work out of them, he added, was through humiliation.
据三位因讨论保密对话而要求匿名的人士透露，他曾对许多下属表示，他们已经太富有了，以至于他无法仅仅用金钱来激励他们。他还说，能从他们身上榨取更多工作成果的唯一方法就是通过羞辱。

This was an extension of a philosophy that went back decades. Mr. Huang had for years been berating his employees, documents and interviews show. His tongue lashings were savage and inventive. He told one executive that his mother should have aborted him, according to one witness. He said he would rip both arms off a subordinate and beat the person over the head to death with them. And he told another employee he would rip off the top of their head and “pee on your brain.”
这是其可追溯至几十年前的管理理念的延伸。文件和采访显示，黄仁勋多年来一直斥责员工。他的严厉斥责既野蛮又花样百出。据一位目击者称，他曾对一位高管说，他母亲当年就该把他打掉。他说他会扯下某位下属的双臂，用它们来敲打他的头，把他活活打死。他还对另一位员工说，他会掀开他们的头盖骨，“在你的脑子上撒尿”。

The tirades were a centerpiece of the culture at Nvidia throughout its meteoric rise to a $5 trillion company and cornerstone of the artificial intelligence revolution. They were also foundational to Mr. Huang’s management style.
在英伟达迅猛崛起为一家市值5万亿美元的公司并成为人工智能革命基石的过程中，这些斥责成为其企业文化的核心。它们也是黄仁勋管理风格的基础。
“I’d rather torture you into greatness, because I believe in you,” he once said.
“我宁愿用折磨来让你成就伟大，因为我相信你，”他曾说。

He has long used humiliation as a tool, excoriating employees in front of their peers with insults, personal attacks and violent comments, while telling them it was good for them or for the business, according to more than a dozen current and former employees, who spoke on the condition of anonymity for fear of reprisal, and to a review of hundreds of pages of court records and other documents spanning more than 20 years. The behavior kept Nvidia’s human resources department busy fielding workplace complaints, but some employees said the department did not take them seriously.
据十多名因害怕报复而要求匿名的现任和前任员工透露，以及对时间跨度超过20年的数百页法庭记录和其他文件的查阅显示，他长期以来一直将羞辱作为一种工具，在同事面前用侮辱、人身攻击和暴力言论严厉批评员工，同时告诉他们，这对他们自己或对公司有好处。这种行为让英伟达人力资源部忙于处理职场投诉，但一些员工表示该部门并未认真对待这些投诉。

Mr. Huang also inspired love and reverence from many of his employees. Thousands have signed a letter asking for his return. Some have tattoos of Nvidia’s logo. Both those who liked Mr. Huang and those who disliked him described Nvidia as cultish. He cultivated loyalty through not just his technical mastery but also acts of personal compassion and praise. But he ruled through fear.
黄仁勋也赢得了许多员工的爱戴与崇敬。数千人签署了一封要求他回归的联名信。有些人在身上纹了英伟达标志。无论喜欢还是反感黄仁勋的人，都形容英伟达带有狂热崇拜色彩。他不仅通过技术专长，还通过个人的共情举动和赞扬来培养忠诚度。但他通过恐惧进行统治。

Mr. Huang’s behavior began long before Nvidia became one of the most valuable companies in the world. In at least two cases originating in the mid-2000s, the company struck settlements with former senior leaders, both of whom had raised concerns about Mr. Huang’s conduct, saying it was unlawful and exposed Nvidia to liability.
黄仁勋的这种行为早在英伟达成为全球最具价值的公司之一之前就已开始。在至少两起发生于2000年代中期的事件中，该公司与前高管达成了和解，两人均对黄仁勋的行为提出过担忧，称其不合法，使英伟达面临法律责任。

Michael Winston, a former senior vice president of human resources, threatened to sue Nvidia in 2005, saying that he had been fired after objecting to Mr. Huang’s conduct, which he described as “the most verbally abusive, threatening and intimidating behavior” he had witnessed in his career. Mr. Huang “thinks he can get away with anything,” Mr. Winston wrote in notes he made around that time, which were reviewed by The New York Times.
前人力资源高级副总裁迈克尔·温斯顿在2005年曾威胁起诉英伟达，称他在反对黄仁勋的行为后被解雇，他将这些行为描述为他在职业生涯中见过的“最具言语辱骂、威胁和恐吓性质的行为”。黄仁勋“认为他可以为所欲为而不用承担后果”，温斯顿在当时的笔记中写道，《纽约时报》查阅了这些笔记。
迈克尔·温斯顿，摄于2011年。
Nvidia reached a confidential settlement agreement with Mr. Winston for more than $1 million, which has not been previously reported.
英伟达与温斯顿达成了一项超过100万美元的保密和解协议，此事此前未见报道。

Mr. Huang resigned from Nvidia last week, after revelations of multiple extramarital relationships, including one with a subordinate and another with a woman whom U.S. intelligence believes to be a Chinese intelligence asset. But his imprint remains on the culture of the company he co-founded in 1993.
在被曝出与多人——包括与一名下属以及与一名被美国情报部门认为是中国情报线人的女子——存在婚外情之后，黄仁勋上周从英伟达辞职。但他依然在这家他于1993年联合创立的公司的文化上留有印记。

Some managers followed Mr. Huang’s lead, six current and former employees said — including his own daughter, Madison, who as his de facto chief of staff often yelled at people, including executives senior to her. (She continues to work at Nvidia.)
六名现任和前任员工表示，一些管理人员效仿了黄仁勋的做法——包括他本人的女儿黄敏珊，她作为他事实上的幕僚长经常对他人大吼大叫，包括对职级比她高的高管。（她目前仍在英伟达工作。）

Mr. Huang denied Mr. Winston’s allegations in a statement from his spokesman, John Fisher, saying they are from an employee who was fired. They are “fabrications that are now impossible to disprove specifically, and the thousands of Nvidia employees who continue to speak out for Jensen show they’re false,” Mr. Fisher said. Mr. Fisher declined to answer other questions regarding Mr. Huang’s behavior.
黄仁勋通过其发言人约翰·费舍尔发表声明，否认了温斯顿的指控，称这些指控来自一名被解雇的员工。费舍尔表示，这些是“现在无法具体证伪的捏造，成千上万继续为黄仁勋发声的英伟达员工证明了这些是虚假的”。费舍尔拒绝回答有关黄仁勋行为的其他问题。

Nvidia declined to comment. Its board and Colette Kress, its interim chief executive, must now decide if the company will continue in the mold of Mr. Huang or forge a new way forward. She will do so in the face of pressure from Mr. Huang and his supporters, who are agitating for his return to the company. Mr. Huang once belittled Ms. Kress in a meeting with top executives, The Wall Street Journal reported.
英伟达拒绝置评。其董事会和临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯现在必须决定，公司是继续维持黄仁勋的模式，还是开辟一条新的前进道路。她将在黄仁勋及其支持者的压力下做出决定，这些人正在鼓动他重返公司。据《华尔街日报》报道，黄仁勋曾在一个高管会议上贬低过克雷斯。
Harvey C. Jones, the chair of Nvidia’s board, said Tuesday that it “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as C.E.O.” Earlier this month, the board opened an investigation into Mr. Huang.
英伟达董事会主席哈维·C·琼斯上周二表示，董事会“不打算恢复黄仁勋的首席执行官职务”。本月早些时候，董事会对黄仁勋展开了调查。
‘It Pained Me’
“让我痛苦”

Silicon Valley has a long history of founders and chief executives with caustic management styles. Steve Jobs, the co-founder and chief executive of Apple, was infamous for screaming at and insulting employees who did not meet his exacting standards. He was also beloved. Employees credited his approach with helping to create culture-changing products like the iPod and iPhone.
硅谷长期以来一直存在以刻薄风格执掌企业的创始人和首席执行官。苹果公司联合创始人兼首席执行官史蒂夫·乔布斯就因对着未能达到其严格标准的员工大喊和侮辱而臭名昭著。他也深受爱戴。员工们认为他的方法帮助创造了iPod和iPhone等带来文化巨变的产品。

Mr. Huang had a similar effect on his staff. He created a flat organizational structure where he interacted with employees at almost every level of the business. He impressed them with his vision for the future of technology, his command of business strategy and the speed at which he tackled and seemed to conquer new areas of importance, leading the company to the forefront of the A.I. boom.
黄仁勋对他的员工产生了类似的影响。他创建了一个扁平的组织结构，据此与公司几乎各个层级的员工进行互动。他对未来技术的愿景、对商业战略的把控，以及他处理并似乎征服重要新领域的速度，给员工留下了深刻印象，引领公司走到了人工智能热潮的前沿。

Many of the company’s senior leaders have worked for Mr. Huang for more than a decade. Some shared Mr. Huang’s belief that mediocrity should be stamped out and excellence pursued, said four current and former employees. If employees didn’t like it, they could leave.
该公司的许多高管已为黄仁勋工作了十多年。四名现任和前任员工表示，一些人认同黄仁勋的信念，即应消除平庸并追求卓越。如果员工不喜欢这样，他们可以离开。
But in the eyes of some, Mr. Huang’s behavior was extreme, even by Silicon Valley standards.
但在一些人看来，即使以硅谷的标准衡量，黄仁勋的行为也是极端的。
众所周知，黄仁勋从不进行一对一会面，而是更喜欢进行小组会面。

In September 2004, Mr. Winston joined Nvidia to lead human resources. A longtime human resources executive who previously worked at Merrill Lynch and Motorola, Mr. Winston was soon taken aback by the disarray of the H.R. department and the cultural norms of Nvidia. This account of his time at the company is based on interviews and Mr. Winston’s notes and emails, as well as drafts of a lawsuit and other legal documents reviewed by The Times.
2004年9月，温斯顿加入英伟达负责领导人力资源工作。作为一名前美林证券和摩托罗拉的资深人力资源高管，温斯顿很快对人力资源部的混乱状态和英伟达的文化规范感到吃惊。关于他在该公司任职期间的这段记述基于采访以及温斯顿的笔记和电子邮件，还有《纽约时报》查阅的诉讼草案和其他法律文件。
In his first days at Nvidia, he learned that two key human resources leaders had just quit and others were on the verge of resigning.
在英伟达的最初几天，他了解到两名关键的人力资源负责人刚刚辞职，而其他人也处于辞职边缘。
That October, at a two-day off-site meeting attended by about 50 employees, Mr. Winston said Mr. Huang unleashed graphic violent threats.
那年10月，在约50名员工参加的一次为期两天的外出会议上，温斯顿称黄仁勋发出了露骨的暴力威胁。
“You have to do this, or I will rip your fucking heart out and stomp on it,” Mr. Huang said at one point.
“你必须这样做，否则我会把你他妈的心脏挖出来踩在脚下，”黄仁勋一度说。

“I watched them helpless, as they were publicly humiliated, indeed tormented, for extended periods of time, by this lunatic!” Mr. Winston said in his notes. “It pained me physically, intellectually and emotionally to be in the room.”
“我看着他们无助地被这个疯子公开羞辱，甚至是被长时间地折磨！”温斯顿在他的笔记中写道。“待在这个房间里让我在身体、理智和情感上都感到痛苦。”

Mr. Winston said other attendees were “terrorized” and pleaded with him to intervene. Days later, he voiced his concerns during a meeting with top executives. One told him that the conduct was typical but could be a liability for the company. Another advised him to “toughen up.”
温斯顿表示，其他与会者被“吓坏了”，并恳求他介入。几天后，他在一次高管会议上表达了他的担忧。有人告诉他这种行为很典型，但可能成为公司的法律隐患。另一人建议他“强硬点”。

Mr. Winston said he then confronted Mr. Huang, warning him that he had “crossed the line” and that mistreating employees could expose Nvidia to lawsuits. He said Mr. Huang dismissed the concerns and defended public humiliation as a “rite of passage.” Mr. Winston said Mr. Huang bragged to him that he subjected new employees to it during their first six months at the company to test whether they would stand for it.
温斯顿称他随后与黄仁勋对质，警告他已经“越线”，虐待员工可能会使英伟达面临诉讼。他说黄仁勋对这些担忧不予理会，并为公开羞辱辩护，称其为一种“成年礼”。温斯顿称黄仁勋向他吹嘘，他在新员工入职的前六个月里让他们经受这种对待，以测试他们是否能够忍受。
Mr. Winston said Mr. Huang told him that he would not stop. “It has good entertainment value,” Mr. Huang told him.
温斯顿表示，黄仁勋告诉他，他不会停止。“这具有很好的娱乐价值，”黄仁勋告诉他。

That November, Mr. Winston was called into a meeting with Mr. Huang and another executive, who then fired him. Mr. Huang told Mr. Winston that he was “not a good fit.” If Mr. Winston sued Nvidia, Mr. Huang said he would make sure Mr. Winston never worked in Silicon Valley again.
那年11月，温斯顿被叫去参加与黄仁勋和另一名高管的会议，随后该高管解雇了他。黄仁勋告诉温斯顿他“不合适”。黄仁勋表示，如果温斯顿起诉英伟达，他将确保温斯顿永远无法再在硅谷工作。
“To say Nvidia fired me because it just was not ‘a fit’ is nothing more than a smokescreen,” Mr. Winston said in his notes. “The real issue,” he wrote, was Mr. Huang’s “unconscionable behavior.”
“说英伟达解雇我是因为不‘合适’，这不过是烟雾弹，”温斯顿在他的笔记中写道。他写道，“真正的问题”是黄仁勋“肆无忌惮的行为”。

In the months that followed, Mr. Winston filed a formal complaint against Nvidia with California’s Department of Fair Employment and Housing, making allegations that he was fired for opposing Mr. Huang’s treatment of employees, including what he said constituted sexual harassment. Mr. Winston then drafted a lawsuit against Nvidia and Mr. Huang.
在接下来的几个月里，温斯顿向加利福尼亚州公平就业和住房部提交了针对英伟达的正式投诉，指称他因反对黄仁勋对待员工的方式而被解雇，其中包括他称之为构成性骚扰的行为。温斯顿随后起草了针对英伟达和黄仁勋的诉讼。
温斯顿向加利福尼亚州公平就业和住房部提交的投诉副本。
But before the complaint was filed, both sides reached a settlement. Neither side admitted liability or wrongdoing.
但在提交诉状之前，双方达成了和解。双方均未承认责任或不当行为。
Mr. Winston rejoined the banking industry, and later blew the whistle against Countrywide Financial Corporation for its conduct during the buildup to the financial crisis. He died earlier this year.
温斯顿回到了银行业工作，后来对美国全国金融公司在金融危机酝酿期间的行为进行了举报。他于今年早些时候去世。

In 2007, Stephen Pettigrew, a former lawyer for the company, sued Nvidia over claims that included age discrimination and retaliation for reporting Mr. Winston’s allegations of sexual harassment. Mr. Pettigrew reported in a complaint filed with the California Department of Fair Employment and Housing that he sought “emergency medical attention for severe nervous tension and anxiety, as a direct result of the actions of Nvidia.”
2007年，前公司律师斯蒂芬·佩蒂格鲁起诉英伟达，诉求包括年龄歧视以及因报告温斯顿所称的性骚扰指控而遭到报复。佩蒂格鲁在向加利福尼亚州公平就业和住房部提交的投诉中报告说，他寻求“针对严重的神经紧张和焦虑的紧急医疗救助，这直接源于英伟达的行为”。

Mr. Pettigrew discussed Mr. Winston’s complaint during depositions for his own lawsuit, citing Mr. Winston’s allegations as evidence of misconduct that exposed Nvidia to legal risk. Nvidia’s general counsel at the time, David Shannon, confirmed during another deposition in the case that Mr. Winston’s dispute was resolved in a pre-litigation financial settlement.
佩蒂格鲁在为自己的诉讼作证时讨论了温斯顿的投诉，将温斯顿的指控作为英伟达不当行为的证据，该行为使英伟达面临法律风险。英伟达当时的总法律顾问戴维·香农在该案的另一次作证中证实，温斯顿的争议是通过诉前财务和解解决的。

Nvidia denied all wrongdoing, and said that Mr. Pettigrew was fired for poor performance. The company countersued, saying that he breached his contract and misused company documents. The case ultimately settled out of court in 2009.
英伟达否认所有不当行为，并称佩蒂格鲁因表现不佳而被解雇。该公司提起反诉，称他违反了合同并滥用公司文件。该案件最终于2009年在庭外和解。
‘Thank You, Jensen’
“谢谢你，黄仁勋”

After Nvidia’s chips were used in 2012 to train an early artificial intelligence system, Mr. Huang concluded that the future of computing would be A.I. Employees recall receiving his email on a Friday saying the company was pivoting its business from graphics to deep learning, a precursor to A.I. He froze hiring for anybody but experts in that field, and Nvidia became an A.I. chipmaker overnight.
2012年，英伟达的芯片被用于训练一个早期人工智能系统后，黄仁勋得出结论，计算的未来属于人工智能。员工们回忆曾在一个周五收到他的电子邮件，称公司正在将业务重心从图形处理转向深度学习——人工智能的前身。他冻结了该领域专家之外的所有招聘，英伟达一夜之间成为了一家人工智能芯片制造商。

A decade later, Mr. Huang’s bet paid off when ChatGPT arrived, kick-starting frenzied interest and investment in A.I. Demand for Nvidia’s chips skyrocketed, and the company’s value soared. Many of the company’s 42,000 employees became fabulously wealthy and were exhilarated to be at the forefront of a technology Mr. Huang referred to as the next Industrial Revolution.
十年后，黄仁勋的押注得到了回报，ChatGPT的出现引发了对人工智能的狂热兴趣和投资。对英伟达芯片的需求飙升，公司市值暴涨。该公司42000名员工中的许多人变得极其富有，并且对自己能处于这项被黄仁勋称为下一次工业革命的技术最前沿感到振奋。

In the wake of Mr. Huang’s resignation, some employees have shared stories of a boss who went out of his way to support them. Last week, Vartika Singh, who works on strategy at Nvidia, recalled Mr. Huang’s support when her sister had brain cancer.
在黄仁勋辞职后，一些员工分享了这位老板曾不遗余力地支持他们的故事。上周，在英伟达从事战略工作的瓦尔蒂卡·辛格回忆，在她的姊妹患脑癌时，黄仁勋曾给予支持。

“Thank you, Jensen,” Ms. Singh wrote in a social media post. “For your guidance, for believing in people and ideas long before the rest of us understood them, and above all, for your extraordinary humanity.”
“谢谢你，黄仁勋，”辛格在一篇社交媒体帖子中写道。“感谢你的指导，感谢你在我们其他人理解之前就相信了这些人和这些想法，最重要的是，感谢你非凡的仁慈之心。”

Mr. Huang’s mix of disparagement and motivation created something akin to Stockholm syndrome, six current and former employees said. The phenomenon, in which somebody held captive develops an emotional bond with their abuser, mirrored their relationship with Mr. Huang, they said.
六名现任和前任员工表示，黄仁勋这种贬低与激励的混合方式制造了类似于斯德哥尔摩综合征的氛围。他们表示，这种被囚禁者对施虐者产生情感联系的现象恰恰能反映他们与黄仁勋之间的关系。

Rather than fire people, Mr. Huang sometimes preferred to further humiliate them. When Ned Finkle, his former vice president of strategic marketing, faltered in a meeting with a major customer, Mr. Huang chewed him out in front of executives from the other company, said two people who spoke anonymously about the private exchange.
相较于解雇员工，黄仁勋有时更喜欢进一步羞辱他们。两名匿名谈论私下交流的人士表示，当前战略营销副总裁内德·芬克尔在与一位重要客户的会议中表现不佳时，黄仁勋当着另一家公司的高管的面将他痛骂了一顿。

Mr. Huang then named Mr. Finkle vice president of external affairs, or government relations. At the time, Mr. Huang considered it one of the least important jobs at Nvidia, the two people said. Mr. Finkle did not respond to requests for comment.
随后，黄仁勋任命芬克尔为外部事务（即政府关系）副总裁。两名人士表示，当时黄仁勋认为这是英伟达最不重要的工作之一。芬克尔未对置评请求作出回应。
Power Plays
权力博弈
Mr. Huang’s tirades continued until the end.
黄仁勋的长篇大论斥责一直持续到最后。

He usually did not meet one-on-one with subordinates because, he has publicly said, such meetings reduced transparency within Nvidia. But top executives considered the move a power play that gave Mr. Huang more control. If anyone disagreed with Mr. Huang, they would have to do so in front of a group. Mr. Huang could then fire back, ridiculing that person in front of everyone else.
他通常不与下属进行一对一会面，因为正如他曾公开表示的那样，这种会面降低了英伟达内部的透明度。但高层管理人员认为此举是一种权力博弈，赋予了黄仁勋更多的控制权。如果有人不同意黄仁勋的观点，他们将不得不在团队面前表达出来。黄仁勋随后可以反击，在所有人面前嘲笑那个人。
Mr. Huang also ripped into longtime leaders in front of their own teams, telling them their boss was incompetent and unqualified, two people said.
这两名人士表示，黄仁勋还会在老牌高管自己的团队面前对他们进行猛烈抨击，告诉团队成员其上司无能且不称职。

In one instance, Mr. Huang went around a room, telling managers he would kill them, according to one person with knowledge of the incident. When he reached a person in their 70s, Mr. Huang said that the person was really old and everyone hoped they would drop dead.
据一名知情人士称，在一次类似情况中，黄仁勋在会议室里走来走去，告诉经理们自己会杀了他们。当他走到一位70多岁的人面前时，黄仁勋说这个人已经很老了，大家都希望这人赶紧死掉。

Mr. Huang also made personal attacks. He once made fun of an executive who had taken his children camping and said he needed to find a more committed employee for the job, according to one person. He often mocked another executive for enjoying aviation as a hobby, two people said.
黄仁勋还进行人身攻击。据一位知情人士称，他曾取笑一位带孩子去露营的高管，并表示他需要为这个职位寻找一位更投入的员工。两名人士表示，他经常嘲笑另一位高管将航空作为爱好。

In 2019, after Nvidia lost a bid to help build a U.S. government supercomputer, Mr. Huang castigated a sales executive in front of government officials for missing out on part of a contract worth hundreds of millions of dollars. The executive then threw his employee badge at Mr. Huang, who said he accepted the executive’s resignation on the spot, according to two people with knowledge of the incident.
2019年，英伟达在竞标协助建造美国政府超级计算机项目中落选后，黄仁勋当着政府官员严厉斥责了一名销售主管，因为该主管错失了价值数亿美元合同的一部分。据两名知情人士称，该高管随后将员工工牌扔向黄仁勋，黄仁勋当场表示接受该高管的辞呈。

Mr. Huang’s behavior rubbed off on other senior leaders at the company, including his daughter, Madison. On one call last year with Nvidia’s marketing team, Ms. Huang repeatedly berated a vice president, who then left the call, according to a recording of the meeting reviewed by The Times.
黄仁勋的行为也影响了公司其他高级领导人，包括他的女儿黄敏珊。根据《纽约时报》查阅的一份会议录音，在去年一次与英伟达营销团队的通话中，黄敏珊一再斥责一名副总裁，该副总裁随后退出了通话。
“I’m having an anxiety attack,” the vice president said. “I’m going to drop off. I’m sorry.”
“我焦虑发作了，”该副总裁说。“我要退出了。抱歉。”
Ms. Huang did not respond to requests for comment.
黄敏珊未对置评请求作出回应。

As Nvidia became the linchpin of the A.I. boom, Mr. Huang’s conduct started to spill outside the company. At Nvidia’s developer conference earlier this year, Mr. Huang moderated a panel with business partners, including Arthur Mensch, the chief executive of the French A.I. start-up Mistral.
随着英伟达成为人工智能热潮的核心，黄仁勋的行为开始蔓延到公司之外。在今年早些时候的英伟达开发者大会上，黄仁勋主持了一场与商业伙伴的讨论会，其中包括法国人工智能初创公司Mistral的首席执行官阿瑟·门施。
Mistral联合创始人兼首席执行官阿瑟·门施3月在圣何塞的一场由黄仁勋主持的座谈会上。
During the panel, Mr. Huang interrupted Mr. Mensch, taking issue with the Mistral chief executive’s French accent, according to footage of the talk.
根据该谈话的视频，在讨论会期间，黄仁勋打断了门施，对这位Mistral首席执行官的法国口音表示不满。
“I want to say it in human words,” Mr. Huang said, after Mr. Mensch tried to explain an A.I. concept. A spokesman for Mistral declined to comment.
“我想用人话来说，”在门施试图解释一个人工智能概念后，黄仁勋说道。Mistral发言人拒绝置评。
Daniel Gutierrez, an A.I. researcher and longtime “Jensen fan” who was watching the panel, said the interaction changed his perspective on Mr. Huang.
当时观看讨论会的人工智能研究员、资深“黄仁勋粉丝”丹尼尔·古铁雷斯表示，这次互动改变了他对黄仁勋的看法。

“I thought in the moment, what is happening right now that’s causing you to attack this poor guy?” Mr. Gutierrez said. “When all the new stuff happened in the last week, I go, wait a minute now. Maybe Jensen isn’t the guy I thought I revered.”
“我当时想，到底发生了什么，让你攻击这个可怜的家伙？”古铁雷斯说。“当上周发生所有这些新事情时，我想，等一下。也许黄仁勋并不是我曾以为我尊敬的那个人。”
Emily Steel是一名调查记者，为《纽约时报》报道商业新闻。她曾揭露多家大型公司内部的性骚扰行为，最近主要关注网约车行业。
Kalley Huang是时报驻旧金山记者，报道科技行业和业内大型公司，包括英伟达和苹果。
Ryan Mac报道全球科技行业的企业责任相关议题。
Tripp Mickle报道英伟达、谷歌和苹果等全球最大的科技公司。他也报道整个科技行业的趋势，包括裁员、生成式AI和机器人出租车等。

items.body:
JONATHAN SWAN, JULIAN E. BARNES, MAGGIE HABERMAN2026年11月23日

2024年，黄仁勋与黄乐在台湾。 Ann Wang/Reuters

The Chinese woman at the heart of the Nvidia scandal kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year while she was carrying out a secret affair with Jensen Huang, according to multiple people with knowledge of U.S. intelligence reports that describe the encounters.

据多名了解相关美国情报报告的人士透露，处于英伟达丑闻中心的中国女子黄乐(Alice Huang)在与黄仁勋秘密保持婚外情期间，曾与中国最高情报机构的一名官员保持了一年多的联系。

The woman, Alice Huang, was in touch with an officer of China’s Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the people with knowledge of the intelligence said. That period overlaps with at least a portion of the time she was in a relationship with Mr. Huang, then the head of the world’s leading maker of advanced artificial intelligence chips.

知情人士称，从2025年春季到今年秋季，黄乐一直与中国国家安全部的一名官员保持联系。这段时间与她和黄仁勋保持亲密关系的时期至少有部分重合。黄仁勋当时还在掌管全球领先的先进人工智能芯片制造商英伟达。

U.S. intelligence agencies have also gathered evidence that Ms. Huang’s business partner, Kang Wei, who was often introduced as her husband, worked with the same Chinese spy agency, the people said.

这些人士说，美国情报机构还收集到证据表明，黄乐的商业伙伴康伟——常被介绍为她的丈夫——也曾与同一个中国情报机构合作。

The extent and specific timing of Ms. Huang’s contacts with the spy agency — and Mr. Kang’s work for the same intelligence service — have not been previously reported.

此前尚无报道披露黄乐与中国情报机构接触的程度和具体时间，也没有报道过康伟为同一情报机构工作的情况。

Ms. Huang’s contacts with the Chinese spy agency last year and up through recent months help to flesh out how U.S. officials came to believe that Mr. Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive earlier this month, was the target of an intelligence operation.

黄乐从去年直到最近几个月里与中国间谍机构的接触有助于进一步说明，为何美国官员会认为黄仁勋是一起情报行动的目标。黄仁勋于本月早些时候辞去了英伟达首席执行官职务。

They correspond not just to the time when he was conducting the affair but also to at least part of the period when Ms. Huang’s company, Megaspeed, was acquiring large amounts of advanced Nvidia chips, some of which went to data centers in Southeast Asia serving Chinese technology companies like Alibaba and some of which are suspected of being smuggled to China.

这些接触不仅发生在黄仁勋与黄乐发生婚外情期间，也与黄乐的公司Megaspeed大量采购英伟达先进芯片的时期至少部分重合。其中一些芯片流向了东南亚为阿里巴巴等中国科技公司服务的数据中心，还有一些被怀疑走私到中国。

Allies of the former Nvidia chief, including President Trump, have sought to minimize the scandal and questioned whether Ms. Huang was spying for Chinese intelligence. But the newly revealed information underscores the continuous contacts that she had with the Ministry of State Security, even as she was in a romantic relationship with Mr. Huang.

包括特朗普总统在内的黄仁勋支持者一直试图淡化这起丑闻，并质疑黄乐是否真在为中国情报机构从事间谍活动。但最新披露的信息凸显了一个事实：即使在与黄仁勋保持恋爱关系期间，她仍持续与中国国家安全部保持联系。

It also helps to flesh out why some American officials have been worried that Ms. Huang’s role is just one element of a much broader push by China in that technological battle. The Ministry of State Security has prioritized focusing on acquiring high-end chips and advancing China’s A.I. ambitions.

这也有助于说明，为什么一些美国官员担心，黄乐所扮演的角色只是中国在这场技术争夺战中更广泛行动的一部分。中国国家安全部已将获取高端芯片、推动中国实现人工智能发展目标列为优先任务。

U.S. officials are investigating the role of Ms. Huang and Mr. Kang in a network of Southeast Asian companies, including Megaspeed, that have been linked to the possible smuggling of Nvidia chips to China, to evade U.S. export control laws. U.S. officials are still working to determine the full extent and duration of their work with Chinese intelligence.

美国官员正在调查黄乐和康伟在一个东南亚企业网络中扮演的角色。这个网络包括Megaspeed在内的多家公司，它们被认为可能参与了向中国走私英伟达芯片的活动，以规避美国的出口管制法律。美国官员仍在努力查明两人与中国情报机构合作的完整范围及持续时间。

The intelligence gathered by the U.S. contains evidence — including shipping records — demonstrating the role of Ms. Huang and Mr. Kang in that network of companies, people with knowledge of the intelligence reports said. The New York Times has previously reported that Ms. Huang and her family have a web of connections to Chinese defense contractors.

了解情报报告的人士表示，美国收集的情报包含运输记录等证据，显示黄乐和康伟在这一企业网络中发挥了作用。《纽约时报》此前曾报道，黄乐及其亲属与中国军工承包商之间存在错综复杂的关系。

本月，在有关黄仁勋与两名女子有婚外情的报道曝光后，他辞去了英伟达首席执行官一职。

Mr. Huang initially described his relationship with Ms. Huang as normal interactions with a business customer. He acknowledged an affair only after The Times revealed last month that Ms. Huang had been identified by the United States as a Chinese intelligence asset and that the Nvidia chief had been picked up on electronic surveillance targeting her.

黄仁勋最初将自己与黄乐的关系描述为与商业客户之间的正常交往。直到《纽约时报》上个月披露，美国已认定黄乐是一名为中国情报机构提供情报的线人，而且这位英伟达负责人的活动也被针对黄乐的电子监控捕捉到，他才承认两人有婚外情。

He stepped down this month after The Times subsequently reported that he had an affair with a subordinate at Nvidia. Administration officials never provided him with a so-called defensive briefing about Ms. Huang, a heads-up that the woman he was in a relationship with had been linked to Chinese intelligence.

此后，《纽约时报》又报道了黄仁勋与英伟达一名下属有染的消息，他随后于本月辞职。政府官员从未向黄仁勋提供所谓的“防范性情报通报”，提醒他与之保持亲密关系的女子跟中国情报机构有关联。

多名了解美国相关情报报告的人士说，黄乐似乎还与中国公安部官员会面。公安部是中国主要的执法机构。

Ms. Huang, Mr. Kang, Ms. Huang’s sister and companies associated with them have emerged as a significant branch of the Chinese effort to build data centers and acquire access to Nvidia chips to train powerful A.I. models. Ms. Huang’s network has been linked to efforts to supply the powerful chips to Chinese-state owned military contractors doing work for the People’s Liberation Army.
黄乐、康伟、黄乐的亲姐妹以及与他们有关联的企业已成为中国建设数据中心、获取英伟达芯片以训练强大人工智能模型努力的一支重要力量。黄乐的企业网络还被发现与向中国国有军工承包商供应高性能芯片的活动存在关联，这些承包商为中国人民解放军承担项目。
Little of the intelligence about Ms. Huang and her network has been provided to Capitol Hill, but lawmakers from both parties are demanding briefings.
有关黄乐及其企业网络的情报很少提供给国会，但两党议员都在要求政府举行情报简报会。

A briefing this month for top lawmakers by John Ratcliffe, the C.I.A. director, and Jay Clayton, the director of national intelligence, was originally scheduled to discuss Iran, but The Times’s reporting on Nvidia led the lawmakers to ask questions about Mr. Huang and Alice Huang. Their answers raised more questions and left some lawmakers puzzled.
本月，中央情报局局长约翰·拉特克利夫和国家情报总监杰伊·克莱顿为国会高层议员举行了一次简报会，原定讨论伊朗问题，但《纽约时报》关于英伟达的报道促使议员们就黄仁勋和黄乐的情况纷纷提问。他们的回答引发了更多疑问，也让一些议员感到困惑。

Trump administration officials postponed a follow-up briefing for top national security staffers scheduled for last Wednesday, in which senior officials were set to share details of the intelligence collected on Ms. Huang.
特朗普政府官员推迟了原定上周三为最高国家安全工作人员举行的后续简报会，按照原计划，政府高级官员将在会上分享针对黄乐收集的情报细节

The intelligence about Ms. Huang was closely held inside the government until The Times reported the existence of the information in late October. Behind the scenes, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who is also the national security adviser, had written a confidential memo, dated March 30 this year, laying out Ms. Huang’s ties to Chinese intelligence.
直到《纽约时报》10月底披露这些情报的存在之前，相关信息一直在美国政府内部受到严格保密。私下里，国务卿兼国家安全顾问鲁比奥撰写了一份日期标注为3月30日的机密备忘录，详细说明了黄乐与中国情报机构之间的联系。
Jonathan Swan是《纽约时报》白宫记者，报道特朗普总统。
Julian E. Barnes为《纽约时报》报道美国情报机构和国际安全事务。他撰写安全相关议题已有20余年。
Maggie Haberman是《纽约时报》白宫记者，报道特朗普总统。

台“数字身份证”一张都没发行仍付10.97亿新台币费用，民进党当局被痛批

据台湾中时新闻网11月22日报道，台湾“数字身份证”政策因资讯安全、隐私疑虑喊停，民进党当局却仍须支付高达10.97亿元的费用。对此，国民党籍民意代表王鸿薇痛批，“数字身份证”至今一张都没有正式发行，内务主管部门2027年度却还编列4870万余元预算，且相关款项要一直支付到2030年，她质疑称“一个错误的政策，可能比贪污更可怕”。

据报道，王鸿薇日前在台立法机构质询时表示，“数字身份证”原本要全面换发，却因资讯安全及个人资料保护问题暂缓推动。依她计算，累计预算数达10.2亿元，但投入大笔经费，最后却连一张都没有正式发行，民众的纳税钱如同打水漂。

台内务主管部门负责人刘世芳宣称，当年因新式身份证存在资讯安全疑虑，导致政策无法继续推动，与印制厂经过协商，最终相关费用合计10.97亿元。“户政司司长”陈永智称，政策暂缓后，民进党当局必须分10年支付印制厂设备折旧等费用，目前已经支付8.49亿元，还有2.48亿元尚未支付，预计要到2030年才能付清。

王鸿薇表示，赖清德于2018年担任台行政机构负责人期间，推动全面换发“数字身份证”，原预计总经费高达48.9285亿元。然而，民进党当局没有做好成本效益及风险评估，就先发包采购设备、投入场地及人事成本，最后政策突然喊卡，导致民进党当局必须持续支付费用。

王鸿薇批评称，政策推动多年，至今没有成果，民进党当局仍年年编列近5000万元支付给厂商，已经花掉8亿多元，未来还有2.48亿元要付，成为长期消耗公款的钱坑。她说，政策失败的代价全部由纳税人承担，却看不到有人负责，赖清德应该出面向岛内民众说明并道歉。

事件在岛内引发舆论关注。台湾“东森新闻云”报道称，有岛内网红在脸书发文称，民进党当局过去曾宣称要把传统身份证升级成“数字身份证”，就像健保卡一样内置芯片，结果政策推动多年，最后却因外界对资讯安全有疑虑而喊卡。让其不满的是，民进党当局并非一开始就决定停止，而是“头洗一半才喊（停）”。相关帖文也引起岛内网民议论，有人留言称“10亿打水漂”“重点是没人为这些错误政策负责”。

items.body:
储百亮, JULIAN E. BARNES2026年11月23日

中国情报机构获取芯片的行动至少已持续两年，相关细节此前未曾见诸报道。 Florence Lo/Reuters

When China’s top espionage agency updated its priorities this year, it added a revealing goal: overcoming Western barriers to technologies that Xi Jinping sees as crucial to China’s rise.

今年，中国最高情报机构调整工作重心时新增了一个耐人寻味的目标：突破西方对那些被习近平视为中国崛起关键的技术所设置的壁垒。

At the heart of that quest are the advanced semiconductors needed to power artificial intelligence, including chips that the United States has barred U.S. companies like Nvidia from exporting to China.

在中国突破西方技术限制的努力中，获取驱动人工智能所需的先进半导体是重中之重，其中包括美国已禁止英伟达等本国企业向中国出口的芯片。

China must “adopt extraordinary measures to intensify the drive for core technologies in priority sectors,” Mr. Xi told the Politburo, a council of senior officials, in January, according to an official text of his speech. “As swiftly as possible, solve the ‘chokehold’ problems holding back development of future industries.”

根据习近平今年1月在中共中央政治局会议上讲话的官方文字记录，中国必须“采取超常规措施，加大重点领域关键核心技术攻关力度”，“尽快解决制约未来产业发展的‘卡脖子’问题”。

The spy agency, the Ministry of State Security, has long been dedicated to eliminating threats to Communist Party rule in China. Now, it has made it a priority to acquire advanced semiconductor chips and gather intelligence about them, according to several serving and former security and intelligence officials from governments outside China in Asia, the United States and Europe.

中国国家安全部长期以来致力于消除对中国共产党统治的威胁。据来自亚洲、美国和欧洲多国政府的现任和前任安全与情报官员称，现在，该部门已将获取先进半导体芯片及收集相关情报列为优先任务。

How China’s spy agency is seeking to obtain advanced chips and intelligence about them has become a central question in the case of Alice Huang. She is a Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. officials say the Chinese agency was working with to spy on Jensen Huang, the chief executive of the American chip giant Nvidia, allegations that were first reported by The New York Times.

中国情报机构如何寻求获取先进芯片及相关情报已成为黄乐(Alice Huang)一案的核心问题。黄乐是中国的一名商界人士，美国官员称，中国国家安全部曾与她合作，监视美国芯片巨头英伟达的首席执行官黄仁勋。《纽约时报》率先报道了相关指控。

Ms. Huang has not responded to requests for comment and China has rejected the claims of espionage as “pure fabrication.”

黄乐没有回应置评请求。中国则否认有关间谍活动的指控，称其“纯属捕风捉影”。

The Chinese spy agency’s campaign to acquire chips, details of which have not been previously reported, has been underway for at least two years, according to the current and former officials. They spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive intelligence.

据前述现任及前任官员透露，中国情报机构获取芯片的行动至少已持续两年，相关细节此前未曾见诸报道。由于涉及敏感情报，这些官员要求匿名。

Among the campaign’s main elements:

该行动主要包括以下几个方面：

• The head of the spy agency, Chen Yixin, who holds the title of minister of state security, created a working team that is leading the effort and reports directly to him, multiple foreign officials said. Mr. Chen has worked under Mr. Xi since they were officials in Zhejiang Province in eastern China, a cradle of China’s high-tech boom.

• 多名外国官员称，情报机构负责人、国家安全部部长陈一新成立了一个工作组领导这项工作，并直接向他汇报。陈一新与习近平的上下级关系始于两人在中国东部的浙江省任职期间。浙江是中国高科技产业的重要发源地之一。

• The group was assigned to help China’s “counter-blockade” work — efforts to overcome export controls imposed by the United States and its allies.

• 该工作组的任务之一是协助中国开展“反封锁”工作，也就是突破美国及其盟友实施的出口管制。

• The campaign includes helping Chinese companies acquire and smuggle advanced chips into China.

• 这项行动还包括帮助中国企业获取先进芯片，并将其走私到中国。

• The group also collects intelligence about the semiconductor sector and its supply chains, according to several officials briefed on the campaign.

• 据多名了解该行动的官员称，该工作组还收集有关半导体行业及其供应链的情报。

2018年，时任武汉市委书记的陈一新，他现为中国国家安全部部长。 Agence France-Presse — Getty Images

In April, Mr. Chen unveiled the new mission. “Deepen the struggle against blockades, and comprehensively advance artificial intelligence innovation, industry development, and applications,” Mr. Chen wrote in a Communist Party journal.

今年4月，陈一新公开提出了这项新任务。他在一份中共刊物上写道：“深入开展反封锁斗争，全面推进人工智能科技创新、产业发展和赋能应用。”

“Focus on tackling the ‘chokeholds’ of critical technologies,” he wrote, and solve the problem of technologies that “cannot be obtained by asking, buying or pleading.”

“聚焦攻克‘卡脖子’关键技术，”他写道，并解决那些“要不来、买不来、讨不来”的技术问题。

“Chen is signaling to the party leadership and his own ranks that his agency is elevating A.I. competition with the U.S. as a long-term, top priority,” said Alex Joske, the managing director of security practice at Garnaut Global, a consultancy firm, who studies the Chinese security apparatus. “He is telling his officers to find more ways to wage this struggle.”

“陈一新是在向党的领导层和他自己的队伍发出信号：他的部门正在将与美国的人工智能竞争提升为一项长期的首要任务，”研究中国国家安全机构的咨询公司Garnaut Global安全业务董事总经理亚历克斯·乔斯克说。“他是在要求手下，要找到更多方式来开展这场斗争。”

A Central Strategy

一项中央战略

The ministry’s campaign is part of a wider push by the ruling Communist Party to overcome Western-imposed restrictions on critical technology. China is determined to close its gap with the United States in the computing capacity needed for progress in artificial intelligence.

国家安全部的这项行动是执政的中国共产党为突破西方在关键技术领域施加的限制而采取的更广泛举措的一部分。中国决心缩小与美国在人工智能发展所需算力方面的差距。

At the top, that effort is being coordinated by the Central Science and Technology Commission. The commission is a secretive Communist Party organ that Mr. Xi established in 2023. This was not long after the U.S. Commerce Department, in late 2022, started banning exports of Nvidia’s advanced chips directly to China, out of concern the chips could help Beijing crack American encryption and design new weapons.

在最高层面，这项工作由中央科技委员会统筹协调。这个行事隐秘的中共机构由习近平于2023年设立。此前不久，即2022年底，美国商务部开始禁止向中国直接出口英伟达的先进芯片，原因是担心这些芯片可能帮助北京破解美国的加密技术以及研发新型武器。

英伟达的Blackwell和Rubin芯片，图为黄仁勋今年3月所作的演示。

The party commission is ranked higher than ministries and is led by Ding Xuexiang, one of only seven members of the Communist Party’s Politburo Standing Committee, its inner circle of power.

中央科技委员会的地位高于政府各部委，由丁薛祥领导，他是中共中央政治局七名常委之一，这个常委会是中共的最高权力核心。

“Computing power is a major indicator of overall national power,” Mr. Ding said in May when he visited energy and computing facilities in Beijing and nearby regions that are part of a planned nationwide A.I. computing network, according to Xinhua, China’s official news agency.

据中国官方通讯社新华社报道，今年5月，丁薛祥视察北京及周边地区的能源和算力设施时表示：“算力是国家综合国力的重要体现。”这些设施是中国规划建设的全国人工智能算力网的一部分。

Mr. Xi created the commission to better marshal the country’s scientists, institutes and labs across ministries, and companies, for national priorities such as achieving technological self-reliance.

习近平设立中央科技委员会，是为了更好地统筹各部委、企业以及科研机构和实验室的力量，服务于实现科技自立自强等国家优先事项。

The Commission rarely surfaces in Chinese news reports; its budgets and plans are not made public. But it has become an engine of Mr. Xi’s plans for technological pre-eminence, said Christopher K. Johnson, a former Central Intelligence Agency analyst focused on China. The director of the commission, Mr. Ding, has long been a close aide to Mr. Xi and is also a vice premier overseeing science and technology policy.

该委员会很少出现在中国新闻报道中；其预算和规划也不对外公开。但前美国中央情报局中国问题分析师张克斯(Christopher K. Johnson)表示，它已成为习近平推动中国取得技术领先地位的重要力量。该委员会主任丁薛祥长期以来是习近平的亲信，同时也是负责科技政策的副总理。

The Spy Agency’s ‘Anti-Blockade Struggle’

情报机构的“反封锁斗争”

China’s espionage service and other parts of the government have for decades pursued technology and research from abroad, using both open and illicit methods. But under Mr. Xi, that effort assumed greater urgency, with more top-level coordination, including in artificial intelligence, several experts said.

几十年来，中国的情报机构和其他政府部门一直通过公开及非法手段获取国外技术和研究成果。但多名专家表示，在习近平上台后，这项工作变得更加紧迫，最高层的协调力度也有所加强，人工智能领域尤其如此。

Throughout this year, Mr. Chen, the agency’s chief, has repeatedly said the “anti-blockade struggle” is one of the key duties of China’s Ministry of State Security.

今年以来，国家安全部部长陈一新多次强调，“反封锁斗争”是该部的关键职责之一。

“Certain countries are going to every length to impose a ‘chokehold’ on China in fields of critical technology,” Mr. Chen wrote in a party journal last year. “Technology competition among the major powers has entered its most intense, most strenuous and most critical phase of close-quarters combat.”

“一些国家千方百计在关键技术领域对华‘卡脖子’，”陈一新去年在一份党刊上写道。“主要国家科技竞争进入最激烈、最吃劲、最关键的‘短兵相接期’。”

中国宿迁的一家半导体工厂。

As American companies, followed by Chinese ones, developed successively powerful A.I. models, officials in Beijing have increasingly recognized the potential for artificial intelligence to threaten their power at home and abroad, said Gregory C. Allen, the founder and chief executive of Decision Tree Research, a firm that specializes in A.I. and other advanced technologies.

专门研究人工智能及其他先进技术的Decision Tree Research公司创始人兼首席执行官格雷戈里·艾伦表示，随着美国企业以及随后跟进的中国企业相继开发出能力越来越强的人工智能模型，北京官员日益认识到，人工智能有可能威胁他们在国内外的权力。

In September, Mr. Chen himself referred to U.S. tech companies and their A.I. models — like Claude Mythos and GPT-5.5-Cyber — as examples of new cybersecurity threats, as he described the risks that A.I. posed to the party’s hold on power.

今年9月，陈一新在谈及人工智能对共产党执政地位构成的风险时，亲自将美国科技公司及其人工智能模型——例如Claude Mythos和GPT-5.5-Cyber——列为新型网络安全威胁的例子。

“China’s senior leadership understands that A.I. is critically, strategically essential, and that leadership in A.I. is obviously related to leadership in semiconductors,” said Mr. Allen, a former senior official at the U.S. Department of Defense’s Joint Artificial Intelligence Center.

艾伦说：“中国最高领导层明白，人工智能具有至关重要的战略意义，而人工智能领域的领导地位显然与半导体领域的领导地位相关。”他曾担任美国国防部联合人工智能中心的高级官员。

Mr. Chen became the state security minister in late 2022, and just over a year later the ministry issued a warning that A.I. was “highly likely in the near future to profoundly transform the national security landscape.” In 2024, the ministry said that its officers were scoring successes against the attempts of “the United States and other Western countries to lock us in at the low-end” of technology.

陈一新于2022年底出任国家安全部部长，仅一年多后，该部就发出警告称，人工智能“很可能在不久的将来深刻改变现有国家安全格局”。2024年，该部表示，其官员有效破除了“美西方国家对我‘低端锁定’的恶毒幻想”，取得一系列斗争成果。

The Role of Businesses and Other Groups

企业及其他组织的作用

China has sometimes used front organizations or researchers to collect information about foreign A.I. technology, said Mr. Joske, the consultant.

咨询顾问乔斯克表示，中国有时会利用掩护机构或研究人员收集有关国外人工智能技术的情报。

“M.S.S. is very comfortable using business covers,” he said, “and it’s very comfortable running people as assets without directly telling those people that they’re working for the M.S.S.”

他说：“国家安全部非常善于利用商业身份作掩护，也非常善于在不直接告知相关人员他们是在为国家安全部工作的情况下，将其发展为情报线人。”

Such covers could include organizations ostensibly focused on academic research. In September, MI5, the British security agency, asserted that a Chinese research institute linked to the Chinese spy agency had drawn in British scientists for research that, apparently unbeknown to the scientists, “directly improves M.S.S. technical capability for espionage.”

黄乐创办的Megaspeed等公司也被视为情报收集的另一种潜在工具。

When China’s top espionage agency updated its priorities this year, it added a revealing goal: overcoming Western barriers to technologies that Xi Jinping sees as crucial to China’s rise.
今年，中国最高情报机构调整工作重心时新增了一个耐人寻味的目标：突破西方对那些被习近平视为中国崛起关键的技术所设置的壁垒。

At the heart of that quest are the advanced semiconductors needed to power artificial intelligence, including chips that the United States has barred U.S. companies like Nvidia from exporting to China.
在中国突破西方技术限制的努力中，获取驱动人工智能所需的先进半导体是重中之重，其中包括美国已禁止英伟达等本国企业向中国出口的芯片。

China must “adopt extraordinary measures to intensify the drive for core technologies in priority sectors,” Mr. Xi told the Politburo, a council of senior officials, in January, according to an official text of his speech. “As swiftly as possible, solve the ‘chokehold’ problems holding back development of future industries.”
根据习近平今年1月在中共中央政治局会议上讲话的官方文字记录，中国必须“采取超常规措施，加大重点领域关键核心技术攻关力度”，“尽快解决制约未来产业发展的‘卡脖子’问题”。

The spy agency, the Ministry of State Security, has long been dedicated to eliminating threats to Communist Party rule in China. Now, it has made it a priority to acquire advanced semiconductor chips and gather intelligence about them, according to several serving and former security and intelligence officials from governments outside China in Asia, the United States and Europe.
中国国家安全部长期以来致力于消除对中国共产党统治的威胁。据来自亚洲、美国和欧洲多国政府的现任和前任安全与情报官员称，现在，该部门已将获取先进半导体芯片及收集相关情报列为优先任务。

How China’s spy agency is seeking to obtain advanced chips and intelligence about them has become a central question in the case of Alice Huang. 根据这项新限制，境外数据中心在向总部位于中国、俄罗斯、伊朗等名单所列国家的企业提供“大规模算力”之前，必须先取得美国政府许可证。新规将在约90天后生效。

袁莉2026年11月23日

Dongyan Xu

A new joke has been making the rounds on the Chinese internet.

中国网络上最近流传着一个新笑话。

Economists have long said that China’s growth has three engines: investment, consumption and exports. The new engines, the joke goes, are raiding officials’ homes, making the rich pay back taxes and collecting social insurance payments from the poor.

经济学家长期以来一直说，中国经济增长有三大引擎：投资、消费和出口。这个笑话说，新引擎是查官员的家、让富人补缴税款，以及向穷人征收社保。

The government needs money to support its rapidly aging population and for costly bets on artificial intelligence. But the economy is in a slump. The result: Chinese people, rich and poor, are feeling the squeeze as Beijing reaches deeper into their pockets to cover its bills.

政府需要资金来支持其迅速老龄化的人口，并投入巨资发展人工智能。但经济正处于低迷状态。结果是：随着北京为了支付各项开支进一步向民众的钱包伸手，无论贫富，中国民众都感到生活压力增加。

Hudson Zhou, a 27-year-old freelance illustrator and graphic designer in the southwestern province of Guizhou, saw work dry up as artificial intelligence replaced human-created designs. Zhou, who uses they/them pronouns, had earned only about $4,500 for the year by the end of October — about half as much as in 2025 — but they owe more this year toward the government pension program.

27岁的自由插画师和平面设计师哈德森·周（音）居住在西南部的贵州省，随着人工智能取代了人工设计，其工作逐渐减少。周（使用代词they/them）截至10月底今年的收入仅约3万元，大约是2025年的一半，但今年需向政府养老金计划缴纳的金额却更多。

Their pension bill — $1,500 — came out higher than last year because the province raised its minimum contribution for gig workers like Zhou.

哈德森·周的养老金账单——约1万元——比去年更高，因为该省提高了像周这样的零工经济从业者的最低缴费标准。

China’s economy is in the doldrums, and a property bust has gutted local governments’ revenue from land sales, deepening local government debt.

中国经济陷入低迷，房地产市场崩盘导致地方政府土地出让收入锐减，加深了地方政府债务问题。

Workers and employers pay into China’s pension funds, but local governments run them and share some of the cost. Strapped for cash, some have taken money from the funds. In a report released in June 2025, the National Audit Office said 13 provinces had diverted about $6 billion from pension funds to cover government wages and repay debt.

劳动者和雇主向中国的养老基金缴费，但这些基金由地方政府管理，且地方政府分担部分费用。由于资金紧张，一些地方政府从养老基金中挪用了资金。在2025年6月发布的一份报告中，国家审计署表示，13个省份挪用了约406亿元的养老基金，用于支付政府工资和偿还债务。

At the same time, the pension system is under strain because of an aging population. Last year only 7.9 million newborns were born in China, roughly half of the average in the 2000s and 2010s.

与此同时，由于人口老龄化，养老金体系正承受压力。去年中国仅有790万新生儿出生，大约是2000年代和2010年代平均水平的一半。

Beijing also has present-day reasons to encourage people to pay more into the national pension system. If people believe they will have something to rely on in retirement, they might save less and spend their money now, boosting the sluggish economy.

北京目前也有理由鼓励人们向国家养老金体系缴纳更多资金。如果人们相信他们在退休后能够有所依靠，他们可能会减少储蓄，将钱花在当下，从而提振疲软的经济。

Xu Chenggang, an economist at Stanford, calls the government’s all-out push to collect more social insurance self-defeating. “The economy’s original problem is insufficient domestic demand,” he said. “Now the government squeezes ordinary people to plug its fiscal holes, which makes demand even weaker.”

斯坦福大学经济学家许成钢认为，政府全力以赴收取更多社会保险的做法适得其反。“经济的根本问题是内需不足，”他说。“现在政府却挤压普通人来填补其财政缺口，这反而使得需求更加疲软。”

Last year China’s Supreme People’s Court made it mandatory for employers to pay for employees’ social benefits, which include pensions, health care and unemployment. Businesses have long been required to pay into the system and automatically deduct payments from their employees’ paychecks, just as in the United States, but the law was not always enforced. The court’s decision was met with resistance from small business owners who say they can’t afford the costs and skepticism from workers who fear they will never collect.

去年，中国最高人民法院规定，雇主必须为员工缴纳社会保险费，其中包括养老金、医疗保健和失业保险。长期以来，企业一直被要求向该系统缴费，并像在美国一样从员工工资中自动扣除相关款项，但这项法律并非总能得到执行。最高人民法院的这一决定遭到了小企业主的抵制，他们表示自己负担不起这些费用，同时也遭到了员工的怀疑，他们担心自己永远也领不到这笔钱。

This year the Chinese government turned its attention to gig workers, who are estimated by one research center to number some 320 million, or more than 40 percent of the country’s labor force. Only about 70 million of them were enrolled in the basic pension at the end of 2024, according to a government report.

今年，中国政府将注意力转向了零工经济从业者，据一家研究中心估计，零工人数约为3.2亿，占全国劳动力的40%以上。根据一份政府报告，截至2024年底，他们当中只有约7000万人参加了基本养老保险。

People in the gig economy, which is called flexible employment in China, pay their own social security. The government wants them to pay 20 percent on a base income tied to the provincial average wage. That wage is often far above what gig workers earn, and it rises every year.

零工经济在中国被称为灵活就业，从业者需自行缴纳社会保障。政府要求他们按与省级平均工资挂钩的基数收入缴纳20%的社保。该平均工资通常远高于零工从业者的实际收入，而且每年都在上涨。

面对经济低迷，北京正不断向民众索取，以支持中国迅速老龄化的人口。

To get people to pay, local officials have tried cajoling and coercion. In Yichang, in central Hubei Province, the authorities threw a street festival in October with dancing robots, costumed historical figures and social security planners in matching vests. Elsewhere, the state is steering people toward taking on debt to pay for their retirement. Banks in a few provinces, working with local social security bureaus, offer loans so gig workers can keep paying into the pension fund, with the debt repaid from their future pensions. Some cities also let residents pay with Huabei, a consumer credit platform.

为了让人们缴费参保，地方官员们既尝试过劝说，也采取过强制手段。在湖北省中部的宜昌市，当局在10月举办了一场街头节庆活动，现场有跳舞的机器人、身着戏服的历史人物，以及穿着相应马甲的社会保障规划人员。在有些地方，政府引导人们通过举债来参与养老金保险。几个省份的银行与当地社保局合作，为零工提供贷款，以便他们能继续向养老金基金缴费，而债务将从其未来的养老金中扣除。一些城市还允许居民使用消费者信贷平台花呗进行支付。

More ominously, the government has also pledged to mine its data to track down people who aren’t contributing. Beijing’s slogan, “leave no one uninsured,” echoes that of the Zero Covid era, “leave no one unquarantined.”

更为令人不安的是，政府还承诺将利用数据挖掘来追踪未缴费人员。北京提出的参保“不漏一人”的口号，与新冠清零时期的隔离“不漏一人”如出一辙。

“Where exactly are these people?” Li Zhong, a vice minister of human resources and social security, asked at a news conference last month, referring to people who aren’t contributing. “We have to find them.”

“这些人到底在哪儿？”人力资源和社会保障部副部长李忠上个月在一次新闻发布会上问道，他指的是那些没有缴费的人。“还是要通过各种各样的方式把人找到。”

The efforts have drawn widespread criticism on social media. A hashtag on why young people opt out of social insurance drew at least 48 million views on the social media platform Weibo before the topic was blocked in searches.

这些努力在社交媒体上引发了广泛批评。一个关于年轻人为何放弃参保的话题标签，在社交媒体平台微博上获得了至少4800万次浏览量，随后该话题在搜索中被屏蔽。

The Chinese government urgently needs to replenish its pension fund, which experts have said may run out by 2035. It has been raising the retirement age and contribution levels but moving slowly to fix inequalities: Retired government workers receive nearly twice the average pension of private sector retirees and more than 30 times what rural pensioners make.

中国政府迫切需要补充其养老基金，专家表示该基金可能会在2035年耗尽。政府一直在提高退休年龄和缴费水平，但在解决不平等方面进展缓慢：退休政府工作人员领取的养老金几乎是私营部门退休人员平均水平的两倍，是农村养老金领取者收入的30多倍。

For Zhou, the visual artist, payments to the pension fund and for medical insurance would amount to $206 a month, or 46 percent of their $450-a-month salary.

对于视觉艺术家哈德森·周来说，向养老基金和医疗保险的缴费将达到每月约1400元，占其每月约3000元工资的46%。

Zhou decided to join a growing number of Chinese who have stopped paying into the pension system, which means they won’t get money in retirement.

哈德森·周决定和越来越多的中国人一样，不再向养老金系统缴费，这意味着退休后将无法领取养老金。

More concerning for Zhou now is the neighborhood committee that serves as the government’s eyes and ears at the local level.

现在让哈德森·周更担心的是居委会，这个在基层充当政府耳目的机构。

In 2022 the neighborhood committee tagged Zhou in WeChat groups repeatedly, calling on them and other residents to enroll in medical insurance. Its workers called Zhou’s mother to urge Zhou to enroll. China Mobile, the state-owned wireless carrier, sent automated reminders.

2022年，居委会在微信群里反复@哈德森·周，呼吁哈德森·周和其他居民参加医疗保险。居委会的工作人员打电话给哈德森·周的母亲，敦促哈德森·周参保。国有无线运营商中国移动也发送了自动提醒。

The Chinese government has other ways to compel payment. In some of the biggest cities, residents without local registration can’t buy homes or cars or enroll their children in public schools without contribution records.

中国政府还有其他方式强制缴费。在一些最大的城市，没有当地户口的居民如果没有缴费记录，就不能买房买车，其子女也不能进入公立学校就读。

Wang, a 24-year-old trainee lawyer in Sichuan Province, has no choice to opt out. (She asked to be identified by only her family name, for fear of government retribution.)

在四川省工作的24岁实习律师王女士（音）却没有退出的选择。（由于害怕政府的报复，她要求只透露自己的姓氏。）

She earns roughly $450 a month and said she had to show proof that her firm pays social insurance for her to obtain a necessary trainee certificate. The social insurance siphons off one-sixth of her pay. She’d rather not pay, she said, partly because it’s too expensive and partly because she questions whether the pension system will still exist by the time she’s old.

她每月的收入约为3000元，并表示为了获得必要的见习证书，必须出示律所为她缴纳社会保险的证明。社会保险抽走了她六分之一的工资。她自己宁愿不缴费，部分原因是费用太高，部分原因是她怀疑等她老了的时候，这个养老金体系是否还会存在。

Some wealthy Chinese entrepreneurs say they feel like fatty meat the government takes a bite out of when it gets hungry. In recent years, even local police have preyed on businesses, sometimes with trumped-up charges, and extracted payment for debt-plagued local governments.

一些富有的中国企业家表示，他们感觉自己就像一块肥肉，政府饿了就会来啃上一口。近年来，甚至地方警察也对企业下手，有时甚至捏造罪名，以此为债务缠身的地方政府榨取资金。

In July Beijing issued a new rule that demands wealthy Chinese to pay taxes on assets they hold in offshore trusts. Bill, an entrepreneur I’ve known for more than a decade, expects to owe tens of millions of dollars.

今年7月，北京发布了一项新规定，要求富有的中国人对其在离岸信托中持有的资产纳税。比尔是一位我认识十多年的企业家，他预计自己需缴纳数千万美元的税款。

Over breakfast overlooking the Imperial Palace in central Tokyo, Bill, who asked to be identified by his English first name because he feared government repercussions, described his confusion and resignation.

在东京市中心一家可俯瞰皇居的餐厅吃早餐时，比尔（因担心政府报复，他要求仅使用英文名字）描述了自己的困惑和无奈。

He has lived in Hong Kong for more than a decade, holds a Hong Kong passport and says he has paid taxes there for years. Under the new rule, he said, none of that may matter.

他在香港生活了十多年，持有香港护照，并表示他已经在那里纳税多年。他说，根据新规定，这些可能都不重要了。

He fears making the payment would amount to accepting Chinese tax residency, leaving his income and investments outside China open to taxation later.

他担心，一旦缴纳税款，就等于承认了中国的税务居民身份，从而使他在中国境外的收入和投资日后也可能被征税。

“Being born in China has become original sin,” he said.

“生在中国已经成了原罪，”他说。

袁莉为《纽约时报》撰写“新新世界”专栏，专注中国及亚洲科技、商业和政治交叉议题。

今年，中国政府将注意力转向了零工经济从业者，据一家研究中心估计，零工人数约为3.2亿，占全国劳动力的40%以上。根据一份政府报告，截至2024年底，他们当中只有约7000万人参加了基本养老保险。

People in the gig economy, which is called flexible employment in China, pay their own social security. The government wants them to pay 20 percent on a base income tied to the provincial average wage. That wage is often far above what gig workers earn, and it rises every year.
零工经济在中国被称为灵活就业，从业者需自行缴纳社会保障。政府要求他们按与省级平均工资挂钩的基数收入缴纳20%的社保。该平均工资通常远高于零工从业者的实际收入，而且每年都在上涨。
面对经济低迷，北京正不断向民众索取，以支持中国迅速老龄化的人口。

To get people to pay, local officials have tried cajoling and coercion. In Yichang, in central Hubei Province, the authorities threw a street festival in October with dancing robots, costumed historical figures and social security planners in matching vests. Elsewhere, the state is steering people toward taking on debt to pay for their retirement. Banks in a few provinces, working with local social security bureaus, offer loans so gig workers can keep paying into the pension fund, with the debt repaid from their future pensions. Some cities also let residents pay with Huabei, a consumer credit platform.

为了让人们缴费参保，地方官员们既尝试过劝说，也采取过强制手段。在湖北省中部的宜昌市，当局在10月举办了一场街头节庆活动，现场有跳舞的机器人、身着戏服的历史人物，以及穿着相应马甲的社会保障规划人员。在有些地方，政府引导人们通过举债来参与养老金保险。几个省份的银行与当地社保局合作，为零工提供贷款，以便他们能继续向养老金基金缴费，而债务将从其未来的养老金中扣除。一些城市还允许居民使用消费者信贷平台花呗进行支付。

More ominously, the government has also pledged to mine its data to track down people who aren’t contributing. Beijing’s slogan, “leave no one uninsured,” echoes that of the Zero Covid era, “leave no one unquarantined.”
更为令人不安的是，政府还承诺将利用数据挖掘来追踪未缴费人员。北京提出的参保“不漏一人”的口号，与新冠清零时期的隔离“不漏一人”如出一辙。

“Where exactly are these people?” Li Zhong, a vice minister of human resources and social security, asked at a news conference last month, referring to people who aren’t contributing. “We have to find them.”
“这些人到底在哪儿？”人力资源和社会保障部副部长李忠上个月在一次新闻发布会上问道，他指的是那些没有缴费的人。“还是要通过各种各样的方式把人找到。”

The efforts have drawn widespread criticism on social media. A hashtag on why young people opt out of social insurance drew at least 48 million views on the social media platform Weibo before the topic was blocked in searches.
这些努力在社交媒体上引发了广泛批评。一个关于年轻人为何放弃参保的话题标签，在社交媒体平台微博上获得了至少4800万次浏览量，随后该话题在搜索中被屏蔽。

The Chinese government urgently needs to replenish its pension fund, which experts have said may run out by 2035. It has been raising the retirement age and contribution levels but moving slowly to fix inequalities: Retired government workers receive nearly twice the average pension of private sector retirees and more than 30 times what rural pensioners make.
中国政府迫切需要补充其养老基金，专家表示该基金可能会在2035年耗尽。政府一直在提高退休年龄和缴费水平，但在解决不平等方面进展缓慢：退休政府工作人员领取的养老金几乎是私营部门退休人员平均水平的两倍，是农村养老金领取者收入的30多倍。
For Zhou, the visual artist, payments to the pension fund and for medical insurance would amount to $206 a month, or 46 percent of their $450-a-month salary.
对于视觉艺术家哈德森·周来说，向养老基金和医疗保险的缴费将达到每月约1400元，占其每月约3000元工资的46%。
Zhou decided to join a growing number of Chinese who have stopped paying into the pension system, which means they won’t get money in retirement.
哈德森·周决定和越来越多的中国人一样，不再向养老金系统缴费，这意味着退休后将无法领取养老金。
More concerning for Zhou now is the neighborhood committee that serves as the government’s eyes and ears at the local level.
现在让哈德森·周更担心的是居委会，这个在基层充当政府耳目的机构。

In 2022 the neighborhood committee tagged Zhou in WeChat groups repeatedly, calling on them and other residents to enroll in medical insurance. Its workers called Zhou’s mother to urge Zhou to enroll. China Mobile, the state-owned wireless carrier, sent automated reminders.
2022年，居委会在微信群里反复@哈德森·周，呼吁哈德森·周和其他居民参加医疗保险。居委会的工作人员打电话给哈德森·周的母亲，敦促哈德森·周参保。国有无线运营商中国移动也发送了自动提醒。

The Chinese government has other ways to compel payment. In some of the biggest cities, residents without local registration can’t buy homes or cars or enroll their children in public schools without contribution records.
中国政府还有其他方式强制缴费。在一些最大的城市，没有当地户口的居民如果没有缴费记录，就不能买房买车，其子女也不能进入公立学校就读。
Wang, a 24-year-old trainee lawyer in Sichuan Province, has no choice to opt out. (She asked to be identified by only her family name, for fear of government retribution.)
在四川省工作的24岁实习律师王女士（音）却没有退出的选择。（由于害怕政府的报复，她要求只透露自己的姓氏。）

She earns roughly $450 a month and said she had to show proof that her firm pays social insurance for her to obtain a necessary trainee certificate. The social insurance siphons off one-sixth of her pay. She’d rather not pay, she said, partly because it’s too expensive and partly because she questions whether the pension system will still exist by the time she’s old.
她每月的收入约为3000元，并表示为了获得必要的见习证书，必须出示律所为她缴纳社会保险的证明。社会保险抽走了她六分之一的工资。她自己宁愿不缴费，部分原因是费用太高，部分原因是她怀疑等她老了的时候，这个养老金体系是否还会存在。

Some wealthy Chinese entrepreneurs say they feel like fatty meat the government takes a bite out of when it gets hungry. In recent years, even local police have preyed on businesses, sometimes with trumped-up charges, and extracted payment for debt-plagued local governments.
一些富有的中国企业家表示，他们感觉自己就像一块肥肉，政府饿了就会来啃上一口。近年来，甚至地方警察也对企业下手，有时甚至捏造罪名，以此为债务缠身的地方政府榨取资金。

In July Beijing issued a new rule that demands wealthy Chinese to pay taxes on assets they hold in offshore trusts. Bill, an entrepreneur I’ve known for more than a decade, expects to owe tens of millions of dollars.
今年7月，北京发布了一项新规定，要求富有的中国人对其在离岸信托中持有的资产纳税。比尔是一位我认识十多年的企业家，他预计自己需缴纳数千万美元的税款。

Over breakfast overlooking the Imperial Palace in central Tokyo, Bill, who asked to be identified by his English first name because he feared government repercussions, described his confusion and resignation.
在东京市中心一家可俯瞰皇居的餐厅吃早餐时，比尔（因担心政府报复，他要求仅使用英文名字）描述了自己的困惑和无奈。
He has lived in Hong Kong for more than a decade, holds a Hong Kong passport and says he has paid taxes there for years. Under the new rule, he said, none of that may matter.
他在香港生活了十多年，持有香港护照，并表示他已经在那里纳税多年。他说，根据新规定，这些可能都不重要了。
He fears making the payment would amount to accepting Chinese tax residency, leaving his income and investments outside China open to taxation later.
他担心，一旦缴纳税款，就等于承认了中国的税务居民身份，从而使他在中国境外的收入和投资日后也可能被征税。
“Being born in China has become original sin,” he said.
“生在中国已经成了原罪，”他说。
袁莉为《纽约时报》撰写“新新世界”专栏，专注中国及亚洲科技、商业和政治交叉议题。

传转转以保密形式申请赴港上市

近日，据报道，二手交易平台转转的运营主体北京转转精神科技有限公司，已以保密形式申请赴港上市，拟募资最高约5亿美元，最快可能于2027年完成上市。

对此消息，新浪科技向转转官方进行求证，截至发稿暂无回应。

公开信息显示，转转是北京转转精神科技有限责任公司运营的二手闲置交易平台，2015年11月由58同城二手频道升级孵化上线，主营手机、3C数码、图书等三十余类目二手交易。2016年业内首创平台居间验机服务；2017年4月获腾讯2亿美元投资；2020年5月6日与二手手机平台找靓机战略合并，成立转转集团，合并后估值达18亿美元，找靓机作为子公司保持独立品牌；2025年，转转集团旗下首家二手多品类循环仓店“超级转转”正式开业。

据介绍，截至2025年底，转转平台累计注册用户超4亿，“上门+门店”回收网络覆盖全国千座城市，线下门店超1500家。
